This workflow describes how often participants answer **Yes** about the earlier
(**distal**) and later (**proximal**) agents in two causal-chain studies. Study 1 is the baseline
chain. Study 2 compares intentional and accidental actions by the distal agent.
The main talk figure shows Study 2 minus the Study 1 baseline for each age,
measure and role. A second summary pools Study 2 child ages and compares participant-level
Distal-minus-Proximal gaps between the Intentional and Accidental conditions.
Raw Yes-response figures remain available as backups. Single Cause adds the one-agent
comparison using children aged 3–6 and all 32 recovered adults. A new synthesis
compares intention effects in Single Cause and Study 2 using children aged 3–6
in both studies. The historical Single Cause N=30 subset remains unidentified.
Three additional stage-grouped synthesis figures show punishment by causal
target, all four Single Cause judgments, and Caused/Lexical role mapping in
Studies 1 and 2. They display raw Yes proportions at ages 3–4, 5–6 and Adults.
This workflow prepares descriptive summaries and cumulative talk figures.
The new Study 1 role-differentiation synthesis additionally fits exploratory
participant-level associations, with and without categorical age adjustment.

**This is a new reproducible reconstruction from available data and documented
design, not recovered original analysis code.** The old verbal plotting scripts
remain missing. The new child exports are the snapshots supplied on September
20, 2026. Study 2 collection remains ongoing, and its adult comparison is an
earlier pilot, not the missing preregistered main adult dataset.

The organization follows the read-only
[counterfactual development Rmd](https://github.com/cicl-stanford/counterfactual_development/blob/a6aabb292549337bdeb220230f3471fd885b8fed/code/R/counterfactuals.Rmd),
[cookie-task Rmd](https://github.com/explanation-lab/cookie-task/blob/295eb985903ec38af4f5ca07df50603729e21d8b/current/code/R/cookie_allocation.Rmd)
and [running guide](https://github.com/explanation-lab/cookie-task/blob/295eb985903ec38af4f5ca07df50603729e21d8b/current/code/R/README.md),
and [cause/burn development Rmd](https://github.com/davdrose/cause_burn_development/blob/48b6aa48e3dad0f3a991e0f5a4842563bfdcbb94/code/R/main.Rmd).
Local reference revisions were respectively `a6aabb2`, `295eb98`, and `48b6aa4`.
We follow cookie-task's principle of selecting one attempt per child and
computing summaries once for all builds. We do not import its study-specific
eligibility rules or the reference projects' inferential models.

## Scope and decisions to review

The Study 1 and Study 2 child preregistration documents require complete test responses from
children aged 3–9 who answer without help. They also specify the first 30
eligible children per age cell (per condition in Study 2), ordered by completion
timestamp. **The requested descriptive snapshot below retains all otherwise
eligible unique children; it does not apply those sample caps.** Some cells
exceed 30 and others fall below 30. This is not a finalized preregistered
analysis. The exports provide session creation times, not completion times,
and cannot independently establish whether adults helped with answers.
The supplied eligibility/exclusion flags are respected; behavioral eligibility
and the cap rule still need confirmation for a registered analysis.

Neither child preregistration nor the available study notes specifies how to
choose among repeat attempts by the same child. We therefore use the requested
deterministic reconstruction rule: among otherwise eligible attempts, retain
the most answered test questions, breaking ties by the latest
`date_created_utc`. Never combine trials across attempts. A Study 2 child who
repeats in another condition still contributes only one attempt in total.

# Load packages

Knitting runs code from this file's directory, `current/code/R/`. CSV values are
read as text first, so identifiers and export labels are not silently changed.
No packages are installed by this document.

```{r packages, message=FALSE}
library(dplyr)       # select, filter, join, and summarize rows
library(tidyr)       # move between wide and long tables
library(readr)       # read CSV files
library(ggplot2)     # figures
library(knitr)       # report tables
```

Single Cause has no separate preregistration in the repository. Its section
uses the supplied inclusion/withdrawal flags and audits the current snapshot.

# Helper functions

## Validate labels and recode yes/no

Unknown labels stop the analysis. Missing values are permitted only where we
explicitly allow them, such as the empty Study 2 session placeholder. Missing
responses never become “no”.

```{r response-helpers}
check_labels = function(values, allowed, label, allow_missing = FALSE) {
  if ((!allow_missing && anyNA(values)) ||
      any(!is.na(values) & !values %in% allowed)) {
    stop(paste("Unexpected or missing", label, "- review the input."))
  }
}

yes_no = function(values) {
  check_labels(values, c("yes", "no"), "yes/no response", allow_missing = TRUE)
  case_when(values == "yes" ~ 1, values == "no" ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_)
}
```

## Keep binary responses separate and average scenarios within participant

The input has one row per participant, scenario, measure, and agent: Yes = 1,
No = 0. A response to one agent never changes the response to the other.
“Both” contributes 1 to both role series; “neither” contributes 0 to both.
No relative-distal transformation or endorsement-based exclusion is used.

`participant_means()` averages available Bike/Mirror answers **within each
participant × measure × role**, keeping conditions separate. Its output has one
row per participant and role-specific measure. A person with one available
scenario has the same group weight as one with two. A missing answer affects
only that question; if both scenarios are missing for a role/measure, only that
participant mean is missing. Other roles and measures remain available.

`audit_patterns()` separately labels both/neither/distal-only/proximal-only
patterns. A missing answer or absent partner row is labeled “missing answer.”
This descriptive audit does not supply plotting values or determine inclusion.
The existing session eligibility and repeat-attempt rules remain unchanged.

```{r scoring-helpers}
check_response_rows = function(responses) {
  key = c("study", "population", "participant", "age", "condition",
          "scenario", "measure")
  check_labels(responses$population, c("Adults", "Children"), "population")
  check_labels(responses$scenario, scenario_order, "scenario")
  check_labels(responses$measure, measure_order, "measure")
  check_labels(responses$role, role_order, "agent role")
  check_labels(responses$condition, c("Baseline", condition_order), "condition")
  stopifnot(!anyNA(responses$participant),
            all(is.na(responses$endorsed) | responses$endorsed %in% 0:1),
            !anyDuplicated(responses[c(key, "role")]))
  invisible(TRUE)
}

audit_patterns = function(responses) {
  check_response_rows(responses)
  key = c("study", "population", "participant", "age", "condition", "scenario", "measure")
  responses %>%
    mutate(role = factor(role, levels = role_order)) %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = all_of(key), names_from = role,
                values_from = endorsed, names_expand = TRUE) %>%
    rename(distal_yes = Distal, proximal_yes = Proximal) %>%
    mutate(pattern = case_when(
      is.na(distal_yes) | is.na(proximal_yes) ~ "missing answer",
      distal_yes == 1 & proximal_yes == 1 ~ "both",
      distal_yes == 0 & proximal_yes == 0 ~ "neither",
      distal_yes == 1 ~ "distal only", TRUE ~ "proximal only"))
}

participant_means = function(responses) {
  check_response_rows(responses)
  responses %>%
    group_by(study, population, participant, age, condition, measure, role) %>%
    summarise(scenarios_available = sum(!is.na(endorsed)),
              yes_mean = if (all(is.na(endorsed))) NA_real_
                else mean(endorsed, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}
```

## Participant bootstrap

Each input row is already one participant's mean for a measure and causal role.
Within each plotted age/role/condition group, resample those participants with replacement 5,000
times. The 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles form the descriptive 95% interval. We do
not resample trial rows or pool pilots. The later Study 1 relationship section
separately fits exploratory associations and bootstraps their slopes.
Family/household dependence is not modeled by these participant intervals.

```{r bootstrap-helper}
bootstrap_mean = function(values) {
  values = values[!is.na(values)]
  if (!length(values)) return(tibble(n = 0L, mean = NA_real_,
                                      lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
  draws = replicate(bootstrap_replicates,
                    mean(values[sample.int(length(values), replace = TRUE)]))
  tibble(n = length(values), mean = mean(values),
         lower = unname(quantile(draws, .025)),
         upper = unname(quantile(draws, .975)))
}

summarize_for_talk = function(means, seed) {
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(means[c("study", "population", "participant",
                                   "condition", "measure", "role")]))
  RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
  set.seed(seed)
  means %>%
    mutate(age_group = if_else(population == "Adults", "Adult", as.character(age)),
           measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
           role = factor(role, levels = role_order)) %>%
    arrange(measure, role, condition, age_group, participant) %>%
    group_by(study, population, age_group, condition, measure, role) %>%
    summarise(eligible_n = n(), summary = list(bootstrap_mean(yes_mean)),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    unnest_wider(summary) %>%
    mutate(x = match(age_group, age_labels) + min(child_ages) - 1)
}
```

## Presentation scaffolds and cumulative builds

All figures use the same computed summary rows throughout their builds. Small,
fixed horizontal offsets separate overlapping roles/conditions; they never
change with the number of revealed series. Child means are connected in age
order; adults are a separate endpoint after the child ages, not part of a developmental
line. Lines describe cross-sectional age groups, not within-child change.

The full legends, limits, factor levels, facets, and whitespace are specified
even for Build 00. The theme is set once above; this helper only adjusts it.

```{r presentation-helpers}
talk_theme = function(text_size) {
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = text_size, color = "#242424"),
        axis.title = element_text(size = text_size + 2),
        axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 14)),
        axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 15)),
        axis.line = element_line(color = "#777777", linewidth = .5),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "#777777", linewidth = .5),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = text_size + 3, face = "bold"),
        panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.1, "cm"),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_text(size = text_size - 4, face = "bold"),
        legend.text = element_text(size = text_size - 2),
        legend.key.width = grid::unit(1.5, "cm"),
        legend.spacing.x = grid::unit(.6, "cm"),
        legend.margin = margin(t = 12),
        plot.margin = margin(22, 24, 15, 18))
}

show_build = function(summary, step) {
  stopifnot(length(step) == 1L, step %in% 0:16)
  filter(summary, reveal_step <= step)
}

plot_study1 = function(summary, step = 8L) {
  visible = show_build(summary, step) %>%
    mutate(plot_x = x + unname(study1_role_offsets[as.character(role)]))
  ggplot(visible, aes(x = plot_x, y = mean, color = role,
                      fill = role, shape = role)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, .25, .75, 1), linetype = "dotted", color = "#E0E0E0", linewidth = .45) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed", color = "#888888", linewidth = .65) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 9.5, linetype = "dotted", color = "#C0C0C0", linewidth = .5) +
    geom_line(data = filter(visible, population == "Children"),
              aes(group = role), linewidth = plot_line_width, show.legend = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                   linewidth = ci_line_width, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(size = plot_point_size, stroke = .8, show.legend = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure, ncol = 2, drop = FALSE, axes = "all_x", axis.labels = "all_x") +
    scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = study1_role_colors, limits = role_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = study1_role_colors, limits = role_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = study1_role_shapes, limits = role_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels,
                       limits = c(2.6, 10.5), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .25, .5, .75, 1),
                       labels = c("0%", "25%", "50%", "75%", "100%"),
                       limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(add = .035)) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = '"Yes" Responses (%)') +
    talk_theme(study1_text_size)
}

plot_study2 = function(summary, step = 16L) {
  visible = show_build(summary, step) %>%
    mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order),
           plot_x = x + unname(study2_role_offsets[as.character(role)]) +
             unname(condition_offsets[as.character(condition)]),
           point_fill = if_else(condition == "Intentional",
                                unname(study2_role_colors[as.character(role)]), "white"))
  ggplot(visible, aes(x = plot_x, y = mean, color = role,
                      shape = condition, linetype = condition)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, .25, .75, 1), linetype = "dotted", color = "#E0E0E0", linewidth = .45) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed", color = "#888888", linewidth = .65) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 9.5, linetype = "dotted", color = "#C0C0C0", linewidth = .5) +
    geom_line(data = filter(visible, population == "Children"),
              aes(group = interaction(role, condition)),
              linewidth = plot_line_width, show.legend = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                   linewidth = ci_line_width, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(aes(fill = point_fill), size = plot_point_size,
                stroke = .9, show.legend = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure, ncol = 2, drop = FALSE, axes = "all_x", axis.labels = "all_x") +
    scale_color_manual(name = "Causal role", values = study2_role_colors,
                        limits = role_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_identity(guide = "none") +
    scale_shape_manual(name = "Intention", values = condition_shapes, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_linetype_manual(name = "Intention", values = condition_lines, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(
             shape = 21, linetype = "solid", fill = unname(study2_role_colors))),
           shape = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(
             color = "#333333", fill = c("#333333", "white"))),
           linetype = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = age_breaks, labels = age_labels,
                       limits = c(2.6, 10.5), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = c(0, .25, .5, .75, 1),
                       labels = c("0%", "25%", "50%", "75%", "100%"),
                       limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(add = .035)) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = '\"Yes\" Responses (%)') +
    talk_theme(study2_text_size)
}

save_talk = function(plot, filename, width, height) {
  ggsave(paste0(filename, ".pdf"), plot, width = width, height = height,
         device = grDevices::pdf, useDingbats = FALSE, bg = "white")
  ggsave(paste0(filename, ".png"), plot, width = width, height = height,
         device = ragg::agg_png, dpi = png_dpi, bg = "white")
}

save_builds = function(summary, plot_function, output, width, height, build_names) {
  steps = seq_along(build_names) - 1L
  stopifnot(identical(show_build(summary, max(steps)), summary))
  builds = lapply(steps, function(step) plot_function(summary, step))
  for (step in steps) {
    save_talk(builds[[step + 1L]], file.path(output, "builds", build_names[step + 1L]),
              width, height)
  }
  names(builds) = build_names
  builds
}
```

# Study 1 — baseline causal chains

## Adults

### Data

The preregistered adult CSV has one row per adult and 16 yes/no fields: two
stories × four measures × two agents. `workerid` contains the existing screened
opaque participant code. All 100 adults are retained; this file has no error
flags or missing test responses. Adult chronological ages are not supplied.

### Read

```{r study1-adults-read}
df.study1.adults.raw = read_csv(
  "../../data/study1_baseline_causal_chains/adults/chains_baseline_full_run-responses.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
stopifnot(nrow(df.study1.adults.raw) == 100L,
          !anyDuplicated(df.study1.adults.raw$workerid),
          all(is.na(df.study1.adults.raw$error)),
          all(df.study1.adults.raw$proliferate.condition == "all"))
```

### Wrangle

The materials establish roles independently in each story. In
`../experiments/study1_baseline_causal_chains/children/slides/chains.pptx`,
slide 6 has Andy run into Suzy, who falls into the fence. Slides 21–30 have
Sophia frighten Bobby, who falls into the mirror. The adult slides tell the
same stories, and `adults/js/trial.js` maps each character to its question
image. Thus Andy and Sophia are distal; Suzy and Bobby are proximal. Randomized
question order does not change these roles. Study 1 is labeled Baseline despite
an unused/misleading `condition_type = "intentional"` constant in the saved
adult HTML; the dataset's condition is `all` and the baseline stories have no
between-participant intention manipulation.

The lookup below states those roles explicitly. `cause` becomes Caused and
`simple` becomes Lexical. Reshaping changes each adult row into 16 response rows.

```{r study1-adults-wrangle}
df.story.roles = tribble(
  ~scenario_key, ~character, ~scenario, ~role,
  "bike", "andy", "Bike", "Distal",
  "bike", "suzy", "Bike", "Proximal",
  "mirror", "bobby", "Mirror", "Proximal",
  "mirror", "sophia", "Mirror", "Distal")
df.adult.measures = tibble(question = c("cause", "simple", "fault", "punish"),
                          measure = measure_order)
df.adult.questions = crossing(df.story.roles, df.adult.measures) %>%
  mutate(field = paste(scenario_key, question, character, sep = "_"))

stopifnot(setequal(names(df.study1.adults.raw),
                  c("workerid", "proliferate.condition", "error", df.adult.questions$field)))
df.study1.adults.responses = df.study1.adults.raw %>%
  select(workerid, all_of(df.adult.questions$field)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-workerid, names_to = "field", values_to = "response_label") %>%
  left_join(df.adult.questions, by = "field", relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  transmute(study = "Study 1", population = "Adults", participant = workerid,
            age = NA_integer_, condition = "Baseline", scenario, measure, role,
            endorsed = yes_no(response_label))
check_response_rows(df.study1.adults.responses)
df.study1.adults.patterns = audit_patterns(df.study1.adults.responses)
df.study1.adults.means = participant_means(df.study1.adults.responses)
```

### Checks and sample sizes

```{r study1-adults-checks}
kable(df.study1.adults.responses %>%
        summarise(adults = n_distinct(participant), response_rows = n()),
      caption = "Study 1 adults: participants, not independent trial rows")
kable(df.story.roles, caption = "Verified story-role lookup")
```

## Children

### Data

`exp4_raw_responses.csv` is the current supplied collected Study 1 export,
copied without changing any values. Each row is an answered question, including
two warmups per session. `child_hashed_id` identifies a child;
`participant_hashed_id` is an account and is not the child unit.
`response_uuid` and `response_id` identify an attempt. Hash codes, session IDs,
and exact session times remain restricted research metadata in this private
repository. Final scientific sample acceptance is still subject to review.

### Read

```{r study1-children-read}
df.study1.children.raw = read_csv(
  "../../data/study1_baseline_causal_chains/children/exp4_raw_responses.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
df.study1.children.raw_counts = df.study1.children.raw %>%
  summarise(study = "Study 1", rows = n(), sessions = n_distinct(response_uuid),
            children = n_distinct(child_hashed_id))
stopifnot(identical(df.study1.children.raw_counts,
                   select(filter(snapshot_expectations, study == "Study 1"),
                          study, rows, sessions, children)))
stopifnot(all(df.study1.children.raw$included_in_summary == "no"))
kable(df.study1.children.raw_counts)
```

### Wrangle: validate labels and count attempts

Warmup rows do not enter scientific scores. `included_in_summary` is always no
and is ignored. The exported `completed` flag is not an inclusion criterion.
We count actual answered Bike/Mirror questions and compare them to the recorded
test count. Each session's metadata must be constant across its rows.

```{r study1-children-attempts}
df.study1.children.questions = crossing(
  df.story.roles,
  tibble(question = c("caused", "break", "fault", "punish"), measure = measure_order)) %>%
  mutate(question_type = paste(question, character, sep = "_"))
check_labels(df.study1.children.raw$question_type,
             c("warmup", df.study1.children.questions$question_type), "Study 1 question")
check_labels(df.study1.children.raw$scenario_key, c("warmup", "bike", "mirror"),
             "Study 1 scenario")
check_labels(df.study1.children.raw$response_label, c("yes", "no"), "Study 1 response")
check_labels(df.study1.children.raw$include_in_analysis, c("yes", "no"), "inclusion flag")
check_labels(df.study1.children.raw$true_completion_status, "complete", "completion status")
check_labels(df.study1.children.raw$withdrawn, c("True", "False"), "withdrawal flag")
stopifnot(all(df.study1.children.raw$study == "exp4"),
          all(df.study1.children.raw$eligibility == '["Eligible"]'),
          all(df.study1.children.raw$is_preview == "False"),
          all(df.study1.children.raw$participant_age_years %in% as.character(child_ages)),
          all(df.study1.children.raw$expected_test_questions_n == "16"),
          all(df.study1.children.raw$left_label == "yes"),
          all(df.study1.children.raw$right_label == "no"),
          all(df.study1.children.raw$response_index == if_else(
            df.study1.children.raw$response_label == "yes", "0", "1")))

df.study1.children.attempts = df.study1.children.raw %>%
  distinct(child_hashed_id, response_uuid, response_id, date_created_utc,
           participant_age_years, include_in_analysis, true_completion_status,
           withdrawn, analysis_exclusion_reason, eligibility, is_preview,
           answered_test_questions_n, answered_all_test_questions) %>%
  rename(participant = child_hashed_id) %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(participant_age_years), condition = "Baseline",
         attempt_time = as.POSIXct(date_created_utc, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS", tz = "UTC"))
df.study1.children.test_counts = df.study1.children.raw %>%
  group_by(response_uuid) %>%
  summarise(answered_tests = sum(scenario_key %in% c("bike", "mirror") &
                                  response_label %in% c("yes", "no")),
            warmups = sum(scenario_key == "warmup"), .groups = "drop")
df.study1.children.attempts = df.study1.children.attempts %>%
  left_join(df.study1.children.test_counts, by = "response_uuid", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(eligible = include_in_analysis == "yes" & true_completion_status == "complete" &
           answered_tests == 16L & answered_all_test_questions == "yes" &
           withdrawn == "False" & is.na(analysis_exclusion_reason) &
           eligibility == '["Eligible"]' & is_preview == "False")
stopifnot(!anyNA(df.study1.children.attempts$participant),
          !anyNA(df.study1.children.attempts$attempt_time),
          !anyDuplicated(df.study1.children.attempts$response_uuid),
          !anyDuplicated(df.study1.children.attempts$response_id),
          all(grepl("[+]00:00$", df.study1.children.attempts$date_created_utc)),
          all(df.study1.children.attempts$answered_tests ==
                as.integer(df.study1.children.attempts$answered_test_questions_n)),
          all(df.study1.children.attempts$warmups == 2L),
          identical(df.study1.children.attempts$eligible,
                    df.study1.children.attempts$include_in_analysis == "yes"))
```

### Wrangle: select one eligible attempt per child

One withdrawn session is excluded by the supplied flags. Among the remaining
eligible attempts, sort by answered test questions and then session creation
time, newest first. All eligible attempts here have 16 test answers, so time
breaks the repeat-attempt ties. The output has one row per retained child.
No age-cell cap is applied to this descriptive snapshot.

```{r study1-children-selection}
df.study1.children.eligible = filter(df.study1.children.attempts, eligible)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.study1.children.eligible[
  c("participant", "answered_tests", "attempt_time")]))
df.study1.children.included = df.study1.children.eligible %>%
  arrange(participant, desc(answered_tests), desc(attempt_time)) %>%
  group_by(participant) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
df.study1.children.repeats = df.study1.children.attempts %>%
  add_count(participant, name = "attempts") %>% filter(attempts > 1L) %>%
  mutate(selected = response_uuid %in% df.study1.children.included$response_uuid) %>%
  arrange(participant, attempt_time) %>%
  select(participant, response_id, date_created_utc, condition, age, answered_tests,
         include_in_analysis, true_completion_status, withdrawn,
         analysis_exclusion_reason, selected)
kable(df.study1.children.repeats, caption = "All attempts by repeated Study 1 children")
```

### Wrangle: make response rows and role-specific means

Keep only the selected sessions and their experimental questions. Join the
explicit scenario/character lookup; an unexpected pairing stops the workflow.
Each output row is one child's binary answer about one agent. Average available
scenario responses separately for each measure and role. Pattern labels are
computed only for the audit and never filter or transform plotting responses.

```{r study1-children-responses}
df.study1.children.responses = df.study1.children.raw %>%
  semi_join(df.study1.children.included, by = "response_uuid") %>%
  filter(scenario_key != "warmup") %>%
  left_join(df.study1.children.questions,
            by = c("scenario_key", "question_type"), relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  transmute(study = "Study 1", population = "Children", participant = child_hashed_id,
            age = as.integer(participant_age_years), condition = "Baseline",
            scenario, measure, role, endorsed = yes_no(response_label))
stopifnot(!anyNA(select(df.study1.children.responses, -endorsed)),
          nrow(df.study1.children.responses) == 16L * nrow(df.study1.children.included))
df.study1.children.patterns = audit_patterns(df.study1.children.responses)
df.study1.children.means = participant_means(df.study1.children.responses)
```

### Checks and sample sizes

These Ns count unique children. “Neither” responses remain two valid no judgments.
They are not the number of sessions or independent test trials. Snapshot
expectations below stop a changed input for review; the displayed Ns are counted
from the data, not assigned from those expectations.

```{r study1-children-checks}
stopifnot(nrow(df.study1.children.eligible) ==
            snapshot_expectations$flagged_eligible[snapshot_expectations$study == "Study 1"],
          nrow(df.study1.children.included) ==
            snapshot_expectations$retained_children[snapshot_expectations$study == "Study 1"],
          !anyDuplicated(df.study1.children.included$participant),
          all(df.study1.children.included$age %in% child_ages))
df.study1.children.age_counts = df.study1.children.included %>% count(age, name = "children")
kable(df.study1.children.age_counts, caption = "Study 1 unique retained children by age")
```

## Combined descriptive data

Adult and child schemas now match. Adults have missing chronological age, and
are placed at the separate Adult category only for plotting. Each bootstrap
group receives one available mean per participant, regardless of how either agent was judged or how many scenarios
are available for that particular role and measure. The resulting table is computed once.

```{r study1-combined}
df.study1.patterns = bind_rows(df.study1.adults.patterns, df.study1.children.patterns)
df.study1.means = bind_rows(df.study1.adults.means, df.study1.children.means)
df.study1.summary = summarize_for_talk(df.study1.means, bootstrap_seed) %>%
  # Reveal adults first, then children, within each measure.
  mutate(reveal_step = 2L * match(as.character(measure), measure_order) -
           as.integer(population == "Adults"))
kable(df.study1.summary %>% select(population, age_group, measure, role, eligible_n, n, mean, lower, upper),
      digits = 3, caption = "Study 1: available participant means and bootstrap 95% intervals")
```

## Talk plots

The four panels show Caused, Lexical, Fault and Punish. Set1 red identifies
Distal and Set1 blue identifies Proximal. Both child trajectories are solid
lines; adult endpoints use the same role colors and shapes. The y-axis is the
percentage of Yes responses for that particular agent, from 0% to 100%.
A dashed horizontal line marks 50% in every panel and build. This is an
endorsement percentage, with no comparison to the other agent. Numerical
tables retain proportions from 0 to 1.

```{r study1-talk}
p.study1.full = plot_study1(df.study1.summary)
save_talk(p.study1.full, file.path(study1_output, "study1_yes_responses_full"),
          study1_width, study1_height)
p.study1.full
```

## Talk builds

Build 00 contains only the complete scaffold. Each following pair adds adults
then children for Caused, Lexical, Fault, and Punish. Build 08 uses the same
summary rows and plotting function as the full figure. Every build is saved as
both a vector PDF and a high-resolution PNG in `talk/builds/`.

```{r study1-builds}
p.study1.builds = save_builds(df.study1.summary, plot_study1, study1_output,
                             study1_width, study1_height, study1_build_names)
kable(tibble(build = 0:8, filename = study1_build_names))
```

# Study 2 — intention × causal chains

## Adults

### Data

All four files in `adult_pilot_rounds_unordered/` are earlier pilots. The
preregistered main adult dataset remains missing. We audit each file separately
and use **one** pilot for a talk/reference comparison. No participants are
pooled across files and no scientific values are inferred from an image.

The current intentional and accidental adult `js/trial.js` files use the same
16 response names as Study 1. Their linked stories independently confirm Andy
as the distal bike agent and Sophia as the distal mirror agent. See
`../experiments/study2_intention_causal_chains/adults/slides/break_crack.pptx`:
slides 4/11 and 30–32 describe Andy's action and Suzy falling into the fence;
slides 48/52 and 73–74 describe Sophia's action and Bobby falling into the mirror.
The current code is identified as v4 in the preserved source note, but a
dataset-to-deployment revision mapping has not been recovered. Identical fields
alone cannot establish which exact experiment version generated a pilot.

### Read

Each raw pilot has one row per adult. The loop reads the four explicitly named
files and checks each file's participant keys, fields, and condition labels.
Its output is a named list of separate pilot tables, not a combined sample.

```{r study2-adults-read}
df.study2.pilots.raw = setNames(lapply(study2_pilot_files, function(filename) {
  read_csv(file.path(study2_pilot_directory, filename),
            col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
}), study2_pilot_files)

for (pilot in df.study2.pilots.raw) {
  stopifnot(setequal(names(pilot),
                    c("workerid", "proliferate.condition", "error", df.adult.questions$field)),
            !anyNA(pilot$workerid), !anyDuplicated(pilot$workerid), all(is.na(pilot$error)))
  check_labels(pilot$proliferate.condition, c("intentional", "accidental"), "adult condition")
}
```

### Wrangle and audit the four pilots

This explicit transformation repeats the adult field mapping for each pilot
separately. `simple` is Lexical; each character keeps its verified role.
`proliferate.condition` supplies the between-participant condition. We calculate
role-specific yes-rates, the same outcome displayed in slide 17. Responses are
averaged across scenarios within participant before averaging participants.
Both/neither response patterns do not change the denominator.

```{r study2-adults-audit}
df.study2.pilots.responses = lapply(df.study2.pilots.raw, function(pilot) {
  pilot %>%
    select(workerid, proliferate.condition, all_of(df.adult.questions$field)) %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(df.adult.questions$field), names_to = "field", values_to = "response_label") %>%
    left_join(df.adult.questions, by = "field", relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
    transmute(study = "Study 2", population = "Adults", participant = workerid,
              age = NA_integer_, condition = case_when(
                proliferate.condition == "intentional" ~ "Intentional",
                proliferate.condition == "accidental" ~ "Accidental"),
              scenario, measure, role, endorsed = yes_no(response_label))
})
invisible(lapply(df.study2.pilots.responses, check_response_rows))
df.study2.pilots.patterns = lapply(df.study2.pilots.responses, audit_patterns)
df.study2.pilots.means = lapply(df.study2.pilots.responses, participant_means)

df.study2.pilots.inventory = bind_rows(lapply(study2_pilot_files, function(filename) {
  pilot = df.study2.pilots.raw[[filename]]
  tibble(filename, N = nrow(pilot),
         Intentional = sum(pilot$proliferate.condition == "intentional"),
         Accidental = sum(pilot$proliferate.condition == "accidental"),
         available_fields = paste(names(pilot), collapse = ", "))
}))
df.study2.pilots.audit = bind_rows(lapply(study2_pilot_files, function(filename) {
  df.study2.pilots.means[[filename]] %>%
    group_by(condition, measure, role) %>%
    summarise(eligible_n = n(), contributing_n = sum(!is.na(yes_mean)),
              yes_mean = mean(yes_mean, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(filename = filename, .before = 1)
}))
kable(df.study2.pilots.inventory, caption = "Separate earlier adult pilots; never pooled")
kable(df.study2.pilots.audit, digits = 4,
      caption = "Pilot comparison: role-specific Yes means after within-person scenario averaging")
```

### Selected talk/reference pilot and limits of the match

We select **`exp2_new_pilot-responses.csv`** (N = 41: 20 Intentional and 21
Accidental). Its adult raw yes-rates visually align with all four panels of
`../../figures/study2_intention_causal_chains/from_lab_talk_deck/slide17_img1.png`
more closely than the other three pilots. For example, the selected pilot's
Intentional Caused distal/proximal rates are .95/.25, Lexical .625/.60, Fault
.975/.025, and Punish .925/.05. The table below gives the exact values computed
from the CSV for both conditions. These are evidence for the comparison choice,
not recovered source-code or revision provenance.

The new figures plot these separate role-specific yes-rates. In particular,
Accidental Punish includes **all 21 adults**: the distal mean is 13/42 = .309524
and the proximal mean is 2/42 = .047619 (two scenario responses per adult).
Neither judgments are zeros for both roles, and are retained. These adult
endpoints visually match the reference, although its generating script and
exact deployment revision remain unverified. The presentation axes say only
“Adult”; the input's pilot provenance remains documented here and in the guide.

### Checks and sample sizes

```{r study2-adults-selected}
df.study2.adults.raw = df.study2.pilots.raw[[selected_pilot]]
df.study2.adults.responses = df.study2.pilots.responses[[selected_pilot]]
df.study2.adults.patterns = df.study2.pilots.patterns[[selected_pilot]]
df.study2.adults.means = df.study2.pilots.means[[selected_pilot]]
stopifnot(nrow(df.study2.adults.raw) == 41L,
          !anyNA(df.study2.adults.responses$condition))
kable(filter(df.study2.pilots.inventory, filename == selected_pilot) %>%
        select(-available_fields), caption = "Selected adult pilot (not the preregistered main sample)")
kable(filter(df.study2.pilots.audit, filename == selected_pilot) %>%
        select(condition, measure, role, yes_mean) %>%
        pivot_wider(names_from = role, values_from = yes_mean),
      digits = 6, caption = "CSV-derived raw yes-rates for visual comparison to slide 17")
```

## Children

### Data

`exp6_raw_responses.csv` is the supplied September 2026 snapshot. Collection is
ongoing; this file does not establish completion of the registered sample.
The CSV is byte-identical to the supplied download; only its `(2)` filename
suffix was removed. Each row is a question response, with one empty-session
placeholder. Child hash codes identify children; session IDs identify attempts.

### Read

```{r study2-children-read}
df.study2.children.raw = read_csv(
  "../../data/study2_intention_causal_chains/children/exp6_raw_responses.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
df.study2.children.raw_counts = df.study2.children.raw %>%
  summarise(study = "Study 2", rows = n(), sessions = n_distinct(response_uuid),
            children = n_distinct(child_hashed_id))
stopifnot(identical(df.study2.children.raw_counts,
                   select(filter(snapshot_expectations, study == "Study 2"),
                          study, rows, sessions, children)))
stopifnot(all(df.study2.children.raw$completed == "False"),
          all(df.study2.children.raw$included_in_summary == "no"))
kable(df.study2.children.raw_counts)
```

### Wrangle: validate labels and count attempts

**Never filter Study 2 using `completed == TRUE`.** It is False even for usable
sessions. Likewise, `included_in_summary` is no throughout and is ignored.
Use the supplied inclusion flag, `true_completion_status`, actual and recorded
test counts, withdrawal/exclusion information, age, eligibility, and preview
status. All retained sessions must contain 16 answered test questions.
One otherwise eligible session has all 16 test answers but no exported warmup
rows; it is retained. Warmups are not test questions and their absence is not
an additional exclusion rule. The export does not establish why they are absent.

The saved child task explicitly labels proximal/distal roles. Its question
construction is in `../experiments/study2_intention_causal_chains/children/`
`jspsych/chains_intentional_accidental_version.js`, lines 229–250. This mapping
does not infer roles from response frequencies. The three missing group labels
occur only in unusable early attempts, and the one fully blank question row is
an incomplete-session placeholder; neither is turned into a scientific response.

```{r study2-children-attempts}
df.study2.children.questions = tribble(
  ~question_type, ~measure, ~role,
  "cause_proximal", "Caused", "Proximal",
  "cause_distal", "Caused", "Distal",
  "lexical_proximal", "Lexical", "Proximal",
  "lexical_distal", "Lexical", "Distal",
  "fault_proximal", "Fault", "Proximal",
  "fault_distal", "Fault", "Distal",
  "punish_proximal", "Punish", "Proximal",
  "punish_distal", "Punish", "Distal")
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$question_type,
             c("warmup", df.study2.children.questions$question_type),
             "Study 2 question", allow_missing = TRUE)
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$scenario_key, c("warmup", "bike", "mirror"),
             "Study 2 scenario", allow_missing = TRUE)
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$response_label, c("yes", "no"),
             "Study 2 response", allow_missing = TRUE)
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$group, c("intentional", "accidental"),
             "Study 2 condition", allow_missing = TRUE)
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$include_in_analysis, c("yes", "no"), "inclusion flag")
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$true_completion_status, c("complete", "incomplete"),
             "completion status")
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$withdrawn, c("True", "False"), "withdrawal flag")
check_labels(df.study2.children.raw$eligibility,
             c('["Eligible"]', '["Ineligible_Participation"]'), "eligibility")
stopifnot(all(df.study2.children.raw$study == "exp6"),
          all(df.study2.children.raw$is_preview == "False"),
          all(df.study2.children.raw$participant_age_years %in% as.character(child_ages)),
          all(df.study2.children.raw$expected_test_questions_n == "16"),
          all(!is.na(df.study2.children.raw$group) |
                df.study2.children.raw$include_in_analysis == "no"),
          all(!is.na(df.study2.children.raw$question_type) |
                df.study2.children.raw$true_completion_status == "incomplete"))
df.study2.children.recorded = filter(df.study2.children.raw, !is.na(response_label))
stopifnot(all(df.study2.children.recorded$left_label == "yes"),
          all(df.study2.children.recorded$right_label == "no"),
          all(df.study2.children.recorded$response_index == if_else(
            df.study2.children.recorded$response_label == "yes", "0", "1")))

df.study2.children.attempts = df.study2.children.raw %>%
  distinct(child_hashed_id, response_uuid, response_id, date_created_utc, group,
           participant_age_years, include_in_analysis, true_completion_status,
           withdrawn, analysis_exclusion_reason, eligibility, is_preview,
           answered_test_questions_n, answered_all_test_questions) %>%
  rename(participant = child_hashed_id) %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(participant_age_years), condition = case_when(
           group == "intentional" ~ "Intentional", group == "accidental" ~ "Accidental"),
         attempt_time = as.POSIXct(date_created_utc, format = "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%OS", tz = "UTC"))
df.study2.children.test_counts = df.study2.children.raw %>%
  group_by(response_uuid) %>%
  summarise(answered_tests = sum(scenario_key %in% c("bike", "mirror") &
                                  response_label %in% c("yes", "no")),
            warmups = sum(scenario_key %in% "warmup"), .groups = "drop")
df.study2.children.attempts = df.study2.children.attempts %>%
  left_join(df.study2.children.test_counts, by = "response_uuid", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(eligible = include_in_analysis == "yes" & true_completion_status == "complete" &
           answered_tests == 16L & answered_all_test_questions == "yes" &
           withdrawn == "False" & is.na(analysis_exclusion_reason) &
           eligibility == '["Eligible"]' & is_preview == "False")
stopifnot(!anyNA(df.study2.children.attempts$participant),
          !anyNA(df.study2.children.attempts$attempt_time),
          !anyDuplicated(df.study2.children.attempts$response_uuid),
          !anyDuplicated(df.study2.children.attempts$response_id),
          all(grepl("[+]00:00$", df.study2.children.attempts$date_created_utc)),
          all(df.study2.children.attempts$answered_tests ==
                as.integer(df.study2.children.attempts$answered_test_questions_n)),
          identical(df.study2.children.attempts$eligible,
                    df.study2.children.attempts$include_in_analysis == "yes"))
```

### Wrangle: select one eligible attempt per child

Twelve sessions fail the supplied analysis flag: six withdrawn, one ineligible,
four with no answered tests, and one with 10 of 16 tests. The four repeated
children with two eligible attempts each lose their earlier tied attempt.
Two of these children crossed conditions; we retain the later eligible attempt
only, without merging or treating the child as two people. The audit also shows
repeated children whose other attempts were ineligible.

```{r study2-children-selection}
df.study2.children.eligible = filter(df.study2.children.attempts, eligible)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.study2.children.eligible[
  c("participant", "answered_tests", "attempt_time")]))
df.study2.children.included = df.study2.children.eligible %>%
  arrange(participant, desc(answered_tests), desc(attempt_time)) %>%
  group_by(participant) %>% slice_head(n = 1) %>% ungroup()
df.study2.children.repeats = df.study2.children.attempts %>%
  add_count(participant, name = "attempts") %>% filter(attempts > 1L) %>%
  mutate(selected = response_uuid %in% df.study2.children.included$response_uuid) %>%
  arrange(participant, attempt_time) %>%
  select(participant, response_id, date_created_utc, condition, age, answered_tests,
         include_in_analysis, true_completion_status, withdrawn,
         analysis_exclusion_reason, selected)
kable(df.study2.children.repeats, caption = "All attempts by repeated Study 2 children")
```

### Wrangle: make response rows and role-specific means

Keep experimental responses from each child's one selected session. The exact
question lookup supplies measure and role; `scenario_key` supplies Bike/Mirror
and `group` supplies Intentional/Accidental. Any unmapped retained value stops
the analysis. The common response schema feeds the same independent
measure-by-role participant averages used in Study 1. Pair labels are only
a descriptive audit, never an input to those means.

```{r study2-children-responses}
df.study2.children.responses = df.study2.children.raw %>%
  semi_join(df.study2.children.included, by = "response_uuid") %>%
  filter(scenario_key %in% c("bike", "mirror")) %>%
  left_join(df.study2.children.questions, by = "question_type", relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  transmute(study = "Study 2", population = "Children", participant = child_hashed_id,
            age = as.integer(participant_age_years), condition = case_when(
              group == "intentional" ~ "Intentional", group == "accidental" ~ "Accidental"),
            scenario = case_when(scenario_key == "bike" ~ "Bike", scenario_key == "mirror" ~ "Mirror"),
            measure, role, endorsed = yes_no(response_label))
stopifnot(!anyNA(select(df.study2.children.responses, -endorsed)),
          nrow(df.study2.children.responses) == 16L * nrow(df.study2.children.included))
df.study2.children.patterns = audit_patterns(df.study2.children.responses)
df.study2.children.means = participant_means(df.study2.children.responses)
```

### Checks and sample sizes

Ns below are unique retained children. No participant is omitted because they
answered no to both agents. Some cells exceed the preregistered cap of 30; this is the requested
uncapped descriptive snapshot. Session creation dates cannot substitute for
the completion timestamps specified by that cap rule without an agreed change.

```{r study2-children-checks}
stopifnot(nrow(df.study2.children.eligible) ==
            snapshot_expectations$flagged_eligible[snapshot_expectations$study == "Study 2"],
          nrow(df.study2.children.included) ==
            snapshot_expectations$retained_children[snapshot_expectations$study == "Study 2"],
          !anyDuplicated(df.study2.children.included$participant),
          !anyNA(df.study2.children.included$condition),

df.study2.children.age_counts = df.study2.children.included %>% count(age, name = "children")
df.study2.children.condition_age_counts = df.study2.children.included %>%
  count(age, condition, name = "children")
kable(df.study2.children.age_counts, caption = "Study 2 unique retained children by age")

        pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = children),
      caption = "Study 2 unique retained children by age and selected condition")
```

## Combined descriptive data

The selected adult pilot and current child snapshot are kept distinct by
population. No adult from the other pilots enters this summary. Bootstrap
intervals resample participant means within the displayed group, exactly as in
Study 1. Plots label the endpoint “Adult”; the pilot source is documented here.

```{r study2-combined}
df.study2.patterns = bind_rows(df.study2.adults.patterns, df.study2.children.patterns)
df.study2.means = bind_rows(df.study2.adults.means, df.study2.children.means)
df.study2.summary = summarize_for_talk(df.study2.means, bootstrap_seed + 1L) %>%
  # Within each measure: Intentional adults/children, then Accidental adults/children.
  # Both causal roles appear together at each reveal.
  mutate(reveal_step = 4L * (match(as.character(measure), measure_order) - 1L) +
           2L * (match(condition, condition_order) - 1L) +
           if_else(population == "Adults", 1L, 2L))
kable(df.study2.summary %>%
        select(population, age_group, condition, measure, role, eligible_n, n, mean, lower, upper),
      digits = 3, caption = "Study 2: participant means and bootstrap 95% intervals; adults are pilot data")
```

## Talk plots

The reference image is 1920 × 1536 pixels. Both new figures keep its 5:4
aspect and 2 × 2 Caused/Lexical/Fault/Punish layout. Study 2 has four series per
panel: Distal/Proximal crossed with Intentional/Accidental. Set1 red
identifies Distal; Set1 blue identifies Proximal, matching Study 1. Intentional uses solid lines
and filled circles; Accidental uses dashed lines and open triangles, with the
same role colors. Legend keys explain role and intention separately.

Values are ordinary percentages of Yes responses, not conditional relative
scores. Both/neither judgments remain in each role's denominator. Child age
means are connected without fitting curves, and adults remain separate
endpoints labeled “Adult”. The y-axis runs from 0% to 100%, with a dashed
horizontal line at 50% in every panel and build. Numerical tables retain
proportions from 0 to 1.

```{r study2-talk, fig.height=12.8}
p.study2.full = plot_study2(df.study2.summary)
save_talk(p.study2.full, file.path(study2_output, "study2_yes_responses_full"),
          study2_width, study2_height)
p.study2.full
```

## Talk builds

All four facets remain present from Build 00 onward. Within each measure,
reveal Intentional adults, Intentional children, Accidental adults, then
Accidental children; both roles appear together. Caused occupies 01–04,
Lexical 05–08, Fault 09–12 and Punish 13–16. Build 16 equals the full figure.
Earlier results stay fixed. Facets never drop, and no summary or bootstrap is
recomputed during build rendering.

```{r study2-builds}
p.study2.builds = save_builds(df.study2.summary, plot_study2, study2_output,
                             study2_width, study2_height, study2_build_names)
kable(tibble(build = 0:16, filename = study2_build_names))
```

# Main talk comparison — change from the Study 1 baseline

Study 1 supplies the baseline judgments for the same causal-chain situations
without an intentional/accidental manipulation. Match groups by **population,
age category, measure and role**. Subtract that Study 1 mean from each Study 2
condition mean: `change = Study 2 proportion Yes - Study 1 proportion Yes`.
The two conditions use exactly the same matching baseline. Never pair people
across studies, pool age groups, or divide by the baseline.

The raw quantity is still each participant's mean of available Bike/Mirror
binary answers for that role and measure. Both/neither remain included, and
missingness stays question-specific. Inclusion and repeat-attempt decisions
are unchanged. The raw figures above remain backup outputs.

The percentage tick labels display changes in **percentage points**: 10% means ten points
more Yes responses than baseline, 0 means the same mean, and -10 means ten
points fewer. This is not percent change relative to the baseline denominator.
Only Intentional and Accidental are drawn; the zero line represents Study 1.

This is a descriptive comparison of different study samples, not within-person
change or an isolated causal estimate of adding intention information. Cohort
or deployment differences can also contribute. In particular, Adult compares
Study 1's N=100 dataset with the selected Study 2 pilot (20 Intentional,
21 Accidental); the Study 2 preregistered adult dataset is still missing.

## Bootstrap both studies

For each age/measure/role cell, independently resample participants from Study 1,
Study 2 Intentional and Study 2 Accidental, with replacement and the original
sample size in each group. Each sampled value is already a participant mean.
Reuse the same Study 1 bootstrap draw for both condition contrasts in each
replicate. Subtract bootstrap means and take their 2.5th/97.5th percentiles.
These are pointwise descriptive 95% intervals that include uncertainty in both
studies; do not subtract the endpoints of the existing raw-mean intervals.

We treat the study samples as independent. Their retained participant codes do
not overlap; the check below stops if this changes. Different anonymization
schemes could still conceal shared people, and household dependence is not
modeled. No confidence statement about an entire trajectory or a difference
between the two change curves is made from these pointwise intervals.

```{r comparison-bootstrap}
bootstrap_draws = function(values) {
  values = values[!is.na(values)]
  if (!length(values)) return(rep(NA_real_, bootstrap_replicates))
  replicate(bootstrap_replicates,
            mean(values[sample.int(length(values), replace = TRUE)]))
}

bootstrap_changes = function(baseline, intentional, accidental) {
  baseline_draws = bootstrap_draws(baseline)
  condition_values = list(Intentional = intentional, Accidental = accidental)
  bind_rows(lapply(condition_order, function(condition) {
    changes = bootstrap_draws(condition_values[[condition]]) - baseline_draws
    if (all(is.na(changes))) {
      return(tibble(condition, lower = NA_real_, upper = NA_real_))
    }
    tibble(condition, lower = unname(quantile(changes, .025)),
           upper = unname(quantile(changes, .975)))
  }))
}

df.comparison.id_overlap = tibble(population = c("Adults", "Children")) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(shared_codes = length(intersect(
    df.study1.means$participant[df.study1.means$population == population],
    df.study2.means$participant[df.study2.means$population == population]))) %>%
  ungroup()
stopifnot(all(df.comparison.id_overlap$shared_codes == 0L))

# One row per matching cell, with separate lists of participant means.
df.comparison.samples = bind_rows(df.study1.means, df.study2.means) %>%
  mutate(age_group = if_else(population == "Adults", "Adult", as.character(age))) %>%
  arrange(study, population, age_group, measure, role, condition, participant) %>%
  group_by(population, age_group, measure, role) %>%
  summarise(baseline = list(yes_mean[study == "Study 1"]),
            intentional = list(yes_mean[study == "Study 2" & condition == "Intentional"]),
            accidental = list(yes_mean[study == "Study 2" & condition == "Accidental"]),
            .groups = "drop")

RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 2L)
df.comparison.intervals = bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(df.comparison.samples)), function(i) {
  cell = df.comparison.samples[i, ]
  bind_cols(select(cell, population, age_group, measure, role),
            bootstrap_changes(cell$baseline[[1]], cell$intentional[[1]], cell$accidental[[1]]))
}))
```

## Compute and save every plotted value

The matching keys below prevent, for example, a distal adult comparison from
using a proximal or child baseline. Means remain in proportion units in the
CSV; columns ending in `_pp` multiply by 100 for the figure's percentage-point
units. The CSV contains all 128 plotted values, their two source means, both
sample sizes, and bootstrap limits, written without display rounding. The
compact table shows the same means to six decimal places.

```{r comparison-means}
df.comparison.baseline = df.study1.summary %>%
  select(population, age_group, measure, role, baseline_n = n, baseline = mean)
df.comparison.summary = df.study2.summary %>%
  select(population, age_group, measure, role, condition, study2_n = n, study2_yes = mean) %>%
  left_join(df.comparison.baseline,
            by = c("population", "age_group", "measure", "role"), relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  mutate(change = study2_yes - baseline) %>%
  left_join(df.comparison.intervals,
            by = c("population", "age_group", "measure", "role", "condition"),
            relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         role = factor(role, levels = role_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order),
         x = if_else(age_group == "Adult", comparison_adult_position,
                     as.numeric(match(age_group, age_labels) + min(child_ages) - 1)),
         reveal_step = match(as.character(measure), measure_order)) %>%
  arrange(role, measure, match(age_group, age_labels), condition)
stopifnot(nrow(df.comparison.summary) == 128L,
          !anyDuplicated(df.comparison.summary[c("population", "age_group", "measure", "role", "condition")]),
          all(is.finite(df.comparison.summary$change)),
          all(df.comparison.summary$baseline_n > 0), all(df.comparison.summary$study2_n > 0),
          all(df.comparison.summary$lower <= df.comparison.summary$upper))
# Use -50% to 50% unless an observed mean requires a wider symmetric range.
# Interval endpoints do not determine this requested display range.
comparison_y_limit = max(comparison_min_y_limit,
                         ceiling(max(abs(df.comparison.summary$change)) / comparison_y_step) * comparison_y_step)
comparison_y_breaks = seq(-comparison_y_limit, comparison_y_limit, comparison_y_step)

df.comparison.plotted_values = df.comparison.summary %>%
  select(population, age_group, measure, role, condition, baseline_n, study2_n,
         baseline, study2_yes, change, lower, upper) %>%
  mutate(change_pp = 100 * change, lower_pp = 100 * lower, upper_pp = 100 * upper)
write_csv(df.comparison.plotted_values,
          file.path(comparison_output, "baseline_change_plotted_means.csv"))

df.comparison.mean_table = df.comparison.summary %>%
  select(age_group, measure, role, baseline, condition, study2_yes, change) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(study2_yes, change))
kable(df.comparison.mean_table, digits = 6,
      caption = "Study 2 minus Study 1: source means and changes in proportion units; CSV includes full precision, Ns and intervals")
```

## Full comparison and cumulative builds

Columns are Caused, Lexical, Fault and Punish; rows are Distal and Proximal.
Purple solid lines with filled circles show Intentional, and teal dashed lines
with open triangles show Accidental. Child age means are connected; the Adult
endpoint stays separate. All eight panels share a symmetric scale and a zero
reference line. The role rows make a third baseline trajectory unnecessary.
The current observed differences all fit within -50% to 50%. Four interval
ends extend beyond this range and are simply clipped at the panel boundary,
without arrowheads. The full interval bounds remain in the CSV. Coordinate
zooming clips only the display; it never deletes the point or its entire interval.

Build 00 is the complete empty scaffold. Builds 01–04 add Caused, Lexical,
Fault and Punish, respectively, for both roles and both conditions. Summaries,
intervals, legend, offsets and geometry are fixed throughout; Build 04 equals
the full figure. The comparison is the main talk figure; the two raw figures
remain available for checking absolute endorsement levels.

```{r comparison-plots, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
plot_comparison = function(summary, step = 4L) {
  stopifnot(step %in% 0:4)
  visible = show_build(summary, step) %>%
    mutate(plot_x = x + unname(comparison_offsets[as.character(condition)]))
  ggplot(visible, aes(x = plot_x, y = change, color = condition,
                      fill = condition, shape = condition, linetype = condition)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#666666", linewidth = .6) +
    geom_line(data = filter(visible, population == "Children"),
              aes(group = condition), linewidth = .8, show.legend = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), linetype = "solid",
                   linewidth = .45, alpha = .55, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    geom_point(size = comparison_point_size, stroke = .75, show.legend = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE) +
    facet_grid(role ~ measure, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = comparison_colors, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Intentional = comparison_colors[["Intentional"]],
                                              Accidental = "white"),
                      limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = condition_shapes, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_linetype_manual(name = NULL, values = condition_lines, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(child_ages, comparison_adult_position), labels = age_labels,
                       limits = c(2.6, comparison_adult_position + .9), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = comparison_y_breaks,
                       labels = paste0(100 * comparison_y_breaks, "%"),
                       expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-comparison_y_limit, comparison_y_limit), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Change from baseline (%)") +
    talk_theme(comparison_text_size) +
    theme(panel.spacing = grid::unit(.6, "cm"),
          strip.text = element_text(size = comparison_text_size + 3, face = "bold"),
          strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
          legend.title = element_blank(), legend.text = element_text(size = comparison_text_size))
}
p.comparison.full = plot_comparison(df.comparison.summary)
save_talk(p.comparison.full, file.path(comparison_output, "baseline_change_full"),
          comparison_width, comparison_height)
p.comparison.builds = save_builds(df.comparison.summary, plot_comparison, comparison_output,
                                  comparison_width, comparison_height, comparison_build_names)
kable(tibble(build = 0:4, filename = comparison_build_names))
p.comparison.full
```

# Study 2 distal-minus-proximal gaps — summary across child ages

This single-panel summary pools **Study 2 children aged 3–9**: 206 Intentional
and 200 Accidental. The adult pilot remains in the raw and baseline-change
figures and is excluded here. First average available Bike/Mirror Yes=1/No=0
responses within each child × measure × role. Then subtract that same child's
Proximal mean from their Distal mean and multiply by 100:

`gap_pp = 100 × (participant Distal Yes mean − participant Proximal Yes mean)`.

Zero means equal endorsement, positive values favor Distal, and negative
values favor Proximal. Both/neither remain included. We never divide by total
endorsement or by the Proximal mean. If either role has no available scenario
responses, that child's gap for that measure is missing; it is not replaced
with zero. The current snapshot has both roles available for every child and
measure. Source role means in the CSV use the same paired contributors.

Each child receives equal weight within condition, regardless of age. The
conditions have different observed age compositions, so this remains an
unadjusted pooled summary, not an age-standardized effect. Roles are paired
within children; Intentional and Accidental are separate groups of children.

## Pair roles within child, then bootstrap participant gaps

Each bootstrap row contains all four gaps from one child. Independently
resample child rows within each condition 5,000 times, keeping the role pairing
and four judgments together. Percentile limits describe uncertainty in each
condition's mean Distal-minus-Proximal gap. Do not bootstrap the roles
independently or subtract their marginal confidence-interval endpoints.

```{r gap-summary-bootstrap}
df.gap.role_means = df.study2.means %>%
  filter(population == "Children", age %in% child_ages) %>%
  select(participant, age, condition, measure, role, yes_mean) %>%
  arrange(condition, participant, measure, role)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.gap.role_means[c("participant", "measure", "role")]))
df.gap.participants = df.gap.role_means %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = role, values_from = yes_mean) %>%
  mutate(gap_pp = 100 * (Distal - Proximal))
df.gap.wide = df.gap.participants %>%
  select(participant, age, condition, measure, gap_pp) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = gap_pp)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.gap.wide$participant),
          nrow(df.gap.wide) == nrow(df.study2.children.included),
          all(is.na(df.gap.participants$gap_pp) | abs(df.gap.participants$gap_pp) <= 100))
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 3L)
df.gap.intervals = bind_rows(lapply(condition_order, function(condition_name) {
  scores = df.gap.wide %>% filter(condition == condition_name) %>%
    select(all_of(measure_order)) %>% as.matrix()
  draws = replicate(bootstrap_replicates, {
    sampled = scores[sample.int(nrow(scores), replace = TRUE), , drop = FALSE]
    colMeans(sampled, na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(draws)))
  tibble(condition = condition_name, measure = measure_order,
         lower_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .025),
         upper_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .975))
}))
```

## Exact values for all eight points

The CSV saves eligible and paired Ns, the paired contributors' two source
Yes proportions, the mean gap and its 95% limits. Columns ending in `_pp` are
percentage points. Percentage tick labels denote these absolute differences,
not relative percentage changes. No display rounding is applied to the CSV.

```{r gap-summary-means}
df.gap.summary = df.gap.participants %>%
  group_by(measure, condition) %>%
  summarise(eligible_n = n(), n = sum(!is.na(gap_pp)),
            distal_yes = mean(Distal[!is.na(gap_pp)]),
            proximal_yes = mean(Proximal[!is.na(gap_pp)]),
            gap_pp = mean(gap_pp, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(df.gap.intervals, by = c("measure", "condition"), relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(population = "Children ages 3–9",
         measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order)) %>%
  select(population, measure, condition, eligible_n, n, distal_yes, proximal_yes,
         gap_pp, lower_pp, upper_pp) %>% arrange(measure, condition)
stopifnot(nrow(df.gap.summary) == 8L, all(df.gap.summary$n == df.gap.summary$eligible_n),
          all(is.finite(df.gap.summary$gap_pp)),
          all(df.gap.summary$lower_pp <= df.gap.summary$upper_pp),
          all(abs(df.gap.summary$gap_pp -
                    100 * (df.gap.summary$distal_yes - df.gap.summary$proximal_yes)) < 1e-12))
write_csv(df.gap.summary, file.path(comparison_output, "study2_distal_proximal_gap_summary_values.csv"))
kable(select(df.gap.summary, -population), digits = 6,
      caption = "Paired Distal-minus-Proximal gaps within each condition: source proportions and percentage-point estimates/95% intervals")
```

## Single-panel paired-point plot

Purple filled circles show Intentional and teal open triangles show Accidental.
A thin neutral connector joins the two condition-specific gaps within each
measure; no line joins different measures. The zero reference marks equal
Distal and Proximal endorsement. Both means and all interval ends fit inside
the displayed range, rounded outward to 25-point steps.

```{r gap-summary-plot, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
df.gap.plot = df.gap.summary %>%
  mutate(plot_x = as.numeric(measure) + unname(intention_offsets[as.character(condition)]))
df.gap.pairs = df.gap.plot %>% select(measure, condition, gap_pp, plot_x) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(gap_pp, plot_x)) %>%
  mutate(intentional_minus_accidental_pp = gap_pp_Intentional - gap_pp_Accidental)
gap_y_lower = floor(min(0, df.gap.summary$lower_pp) / gap_y_step) * gap_y_step
gap_y_upper = ceiling(max(0, df.gap.summary$upper_pp) / gap_y_step) * gap_y_step
p.gap.summary = ggplot(df.gap.plot,
  aes(x = plot_x, y = gap_pp, color = condition, fill = condition, shape = condition)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#777777", linewidth = .6) +
  geom_segment(data = df.gap.pairs,
                aes(x = plot_x_Intentional, xend = plot_x_Accidental,
                    y = gap_pp_Intentional, yend = gap_pp_Accidental),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "#A0A0A0", linewidth = .6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower_pp, ymax = upper_pp), width = .055,
                linewidth = .55, alpha = .65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 4.3, stroke = 1, show.legend = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = comparison_colors, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Intentional = comparison_colors[["Intentional"]], Accidental = "white"),
                    limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = condition_shapes, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(measure_order), labels = measure_order,
                     limits = c(.5, length(measure_order) + .5), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(gap_y_lower, gap_y_upper, gap_y_step),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(gap_y_lower, gap_y_upper),
                     expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression(plain("Distal") - plain("Proximal") ~ plain("(percentage points)"))) +
  talk_theme(intention_text_size)
save_talk(p.gap.summary, file.path(comparison_output, "study2_distal_proximal_gap_summary"),
          intention_width, intention_height)
p.gap.summary
```

## What the summary supports

Intentional has a larger (more positive) Distal-minus-Proximal gap than
Accidental for every measure. The between-condition separation is greatest
for Punish (39.60 percentage points), followed by Lexical (27.95), Fault
(22.88) and Caused (16.20). Fault has a large positive Intentional gap, but
the intentionality-related widening is not especially large for Fault
relative to Lexical. Lexical gaps are negative in both conditions: children
endorse Proximal more often there, although less strongly under Intentional.
These are descriptive comparisons; the pointwise intervals do not formally
test whether the between-condition separation differs across measures.

# Single Cause — one direct causal agent

The Single Cause comparison uses the same Intentional/Accidental manipulation
and four judgments as Study 2, but one agent directly brings about the outcome.
There is no distal/proximal choice or relative-attribution score. This section
adds the supplied `exp7` child snapshot to the shared workflow. Historical
figures, experiment files and adult data are left unchanged.

## Children: read and audit the export

The supplied raw CSV is copied without changing values. `child_hashed_id` is
the participant unit; `response_uuid` identifies a session. Hash codes, session
IDs and session dates remain restricted research metadata in the private repo.
The export has two warmup answers plus eight test answers per session.
`completed` is False throughout and is not an inclusion filter.
`included_in_summary` is a row-level export flag and is never used for inclusion.
The exported `expected_test_questions_n` and `answered_test_questions_n` both
say 2, although actual Bike/Mirror rows show eight answers per session. Their
meaning is unverified; we audit that discrepancy and count actual response
rows rather than using these two fields as test-question totals.

```{r single-read-audit}
df.single.raw = read_csv("../../data/single_cause/children/exp7_raw_responses.csv",
                          col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
df.single.raw_counts = df.single.raw %>%
  summarise(rows = n(), sessions = n_distinct(response_uuid),
            children = n_distinct(child_hashed_id))
if (!identical(as.integer(unlist(df.single.raw_counts[1, ], use.names = FALSE)), c(970L, 97L, 97L))) {
  stop("Single Cause export counts differ from the supplied snapshot; stop for review.")
}
check_labels(df.single.raw$study, "exp7", "Single Cause study")
check_labels(df.single.raw$group, tolower(condition_order), "Single Cause condition")
check_labels(df.single.raw$participant_age_years, as.character(single_child_ages), "Single Cause age")
check_labels(df.single.raw$scenario_key, c("warmup", "bike", "mirror"), "Single Cause scenario")
check_labels(df.single.raw$question_type, c("warmup", "cause", "lexical", "fault", "punish"), "Single Cause question")
check_labels(df.single.raw$response_label, c("yes", "no"), "Single Cause response", allow_missing = TRUE)
check_labels(df.single.raw$include_in_analysis, c("yes", "no"), "Single Cause inclusion flag")
check_labels(df.single.raw$withdrawn, c("True", "False"), "Single Cause withdrawal")
check_labels(df.single.raw$true_completion_status, "complete", "Single Cause completion")
stopifnot(all(df.single.raw$completed == "False"),
          all(df.single.raw$eligibility == '["Eligible"]'),
          all(df.single.raw$is_preview == "False"),
          all(df.single.raw$expected_test_questions_n == "2"),
          all(df.single.raw$left_label == "yes"), all(df.single.raw$right_label == "no"),
          all(df.single.raw$response_index == if_else(df.single.raw$response_label == "yes", "0", "1")),
          all((df.single.raw$scenario_key == "warmup") == (df.single.raw$question_type == "warmup")))
kable(df.single.raw_counts, caption = "Single Cause raw export: rows, sessions and unique children")

# Distinct metadata must reduce to exactly one row per session.
df.single.sessions = df.single.raw %>%
  distinct(response_uuid, response_id, child_hashed_id, participant_age_years, group,
           include_in_analysis, true_completion_status, withdrawn, analysis_exclusion_reason,
           eligibility, is_preview, answered_test_questions_n, answered_all_test_questions) %>%
  rename(participant = child_hashed_id) %>%
  mutate(age = as.integer(participant_age_years),
         condition = if_else(group == "intentional", "Intentional", "Accidental"))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.single.sessions$response_uuid),
          !anyDuplicated(df.single.sessions$response_id), !anyNA(df.single.sessions$participant))
df.single.trial_counts = df.single.raw %>%
  group_by(response_uuid) %>%
  summarise(warmups = sum(scenario_key == "warmup"),
            test_rows = sum(scenario_key %in% c("bike", "mirror")),
            answered_tests = sum(scenario_key %in% c("bike", "mirror") & response_label %in% c("yes", "no")),
            .groups = "drop")
df.single.sessions = df.single.sessions %>%
  left_join(df.single.trial_counts, by = "response_uuid", relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(included = include_in_analysis == "yes" & withdrawn == "False" &
           is.na(analysis_exclusion_reason) & true_completion_status == "complete" &
           eligibility == '["Eligible"]' & is_preview == "False")
stopifnot(all(df.single.sessions$warmups == 2L), all(df.single.sessions$test_rows == 8L),
          all(df.single.sessions$answered_tests == 8L),
          all(df.single.sessions$answered_test_questions_n == "2"),
          all(df.single.sessions$answered_all_test_questions == "yes"),
          identical(df.single.sessions$included, df.single.sessions$include_in_analysis == "yes"),
          sum(df.single.sessions$included) == 96L,
          sum(df.single.sessions$withdrawn == "True") == 1L,
          all(df.single.sessions$analysis_exclusion_reason[!df.single.sessions$included] == "withdrawn"))

# Do not silently select a new repeat-attempt rule if this export changes.
df.single.repeats = df.single.sessions %>% count(participant, name = "sessions") %>% filter(sessions > 1L)
kable(tibble(repeated_child_ids = nrow(df.single.repeats)), caption = "Repeat-child audit (all sessions, including excluded)")

df.single.included = filter(df.single.sessions, included)
df.single.flow = tibble(
  stage = c("Raw sessions / unique children", "Withdrawn and flagged for exclusion", "Included sessions / unique children"),
  n = c(nrow(df.single.sessions), sum(!df.single.sessions$included), nrow(df.single.included)))
kable(df.single.flow, caption = "Single Cause inclusion flow")

if (nrow(anti_join(df.single.ns, single_expected_ns, by = c("age", "condition", "n"))) > 0L ||
    nrow(anti_join(single_expected_ns, df.single.ns, by = c("age", "condition", "n"))) > 0L) {

}

kable(df.single.raw %>% count(completed, true_completion_status, included_in_summary,
```
