## Recode and average within child

Only Bike/Mirror test rows from included sessions enter scores. The 194 raw
warmup rows are excluded, including 192 from included sessions. The withdrawn
session's eight test answers are also excluded. This leaves 768 scientific
response rows. Each child contributes four scenario-averaged scores. Missing
answers would remain missing for that question and never become No; the current
snapshot has both scenarios available for all 384 child-by-measure means.

```{r single-participant-means}
df.single.questions = tibble(question_type = c("cause", "lexical", "fault", "punish"),
                              measure = measure_order)
df.single.responses = df.single.raw %>%
  filter(scenario_key %in% c("bike", "mirror")) %>%
  inner_join(select(df.single.included, response_uuid, participant, age, condition),
             by = "response_uuid", relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  left_join(df.single.questions, by = "question_type", relationship = "many-to-one") %>%
  transmute(participant, age, condition, scenario = scenario_key, measure,
            endorsed = yes_no(response_label))
stopifnot(nrow(df.single.responses) == 768L, !anyNA(df.single.responses$measure),
          !anyDuplicated(df.single.responses[c("participant", "scenario", "measure")]))
df.single.means = df.single.responses %>%
  group_by(participant, age, condition, measure) %>%
  summarise(scenarios_available = sum(!is.na(endorsed)),
            yes_mean = if (all(is.na(endorsed))) NA_real_ else mean(endorsed, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(df.single.means) == 384L, all(df.single.means$scenarios_available == 2L))
kable(tibble(raw_warmup_rows_excluded = sum(df.single.raw$scenario_key == "warmup"),
             included_test_rows = nrow(df.single.responses), participant_measure_means = nrow(df.single.means)))
```

## Adults: use all 32 recovered complete records

The adult CSV has 32 unique participant codes, 16 per condition. All eight
answers are present for every row, and every `error` field is blank. No row
is identified as excluded or incomplete. The source note calls two rows
"likely excluded/incomplete" but provides no IDs or rule. Slide 20 reports
30 adults, 15 per condition. Its embedded plot supplies no participant-level
exclusion information. The saved experiment and conversion code define the
eight questions but do not recover the historical exclusion decision.

We cannot defensibly identify the historical 30-person subset. **By explicit
review decision, the current working plots use all 32 complete adults, 16 per
condition.** We do not fabricate an exclusion rule or reverse-select rows to
match the old slide. This is a documented working sample, not a recovered
historical N=30 analysis. All source rows and historical images remain unchanged.
Adults appear as a separate endpoint; they are not pooled into the child summaries.
See the [adult audit](../../docs/single_cause/adults/ANALYSIS_AUDIT.md) for inspected sources.

```{r single-adult-audit}
df.single.adults.raw = read_csv("../../data/single_cause/adults/single_cause_pilot1-responses.csv",
                               col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
single_adult_fields = c("bike_cause_andy", "bike_simple_andy", "bike_fault_andy", "bike_punish_andy",
                        "mirror_cause_sophia", "mirror_simple_sophia", "mirror_fault_sophia", "mirror_punish_sophia")
df.single.adults.audit = df.single.adults.raw %>%
  mutate(answered_tests = rowSums(as.data.frame(lapply(select(., all_of(single_adult_fields)),
                                                      function(x) x %in% c("yes", "no"))))) %>%
  group_by(condition = proliferate.condition) %>%
  summarise(rows = n(), unique_ids = n_distinct(workerid),
            complete_eight_answers = sum(answered_tests == 8L),
            nonblank_errors = sum(!is.na(error)), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(df.single.adults.raw) == 32L, !anyDuplicated(df.single.adults.raw$workerid),
          all(df.single.adults.audit$rows == 16L), all(df.single.adults.audit$complete_eight_answers == 16L),
          all(df.single.adults.audit$nonblank_errors == 0L))
kable(df.single.adults.audit, caption = "Working adult sample: all 32 complete records, 16 per condition")
check_labels(df.single.adults.raw$proliferate.condition, tolower(condition_order), "Single Cause adult condition")
df.single.adults.responses = df.single.adults.raw %>%
  select(participant = workerid, condition = proliferate.condition, all_of(single_adult_fields)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(single_adult_fields), names_to = c("scenario", "question", "agent"),
               names_sep = "_", values_to = "response") %>%
  mutate(condition = if_else(condition == "intentional", "Intentional", "Accidental"),
         measure = recode(question, cause = "Caused", simple = "Lexical", fault = "Fault", punish = "Punish"),
         endorsed = yes_no(response))
df.single.adults.means = df.single.adults.responses %>%
  group_by(participant, condition, measure) %>%
  summarise(scenarios_available = sum(!is.na(endorsed)),
            yes_mean = mean(endorsed), .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(nrow(df.single.adults.means) == 128L,
          all(df.single.adults.means$scenarios_available == 2L),
          !anyNA(df.single.adults.means$yes_mean))
```

## Age-group summaries and developmental figure

Bootstrap the participant means within age × condition × measure with the
shared 5,000-replicate helper and a fixed seed. Every child receives equal
weight within their age/condition group. The figure uses four panels, 0–100%
Yes responses and ages 3–6 plus an Adult endpoint (16 participants per condition).
There are no empty ages 7–9. A dashed 50% reference matches Study 2; it is a
visual midpoint, not a chance-model assumption. Adults and children are
bootstrapped separately; the existing child estimates and intervals are unchanged.
Intentional uses the existing named purple color, a solid line and filled
circle; Accidental uses the existing teal color, a dashed line and open triangle.
The shared 16 × 12.8-inch dimensions and typography match the raw chain figures.

```{r single-developmental-summary}
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 4L)
df.single.children.summary = df.single.means %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order)) %>%
  arrange(measure, condition, age, participant) %>%
  group_by(age, condition, measure) %>%
  summarise(summary = list(bootstrap_mean(yes_mean)), .groups = "drop") %>% unnest_wider(summary) %>%
  mutate(population = "Children", age_group = as.character(age), x = as.numeric(age))
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 7L)
df.single.adults.summary = df.single.adults.means %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order)) %>%
  arrange(measure, condition, participant) %>% group_by(condition, measure) %>%
  summarise(summary = list(bootstrap_mean(yes_mean)), .groups = "drop") %>% unnest_wider(summary) %>%
  mutate(population = "Adults", age = NA_integer_, age_group = "Adult", x = single_adult_position)
df.single.summary = bind_rows(df.single.children.summary, df.single.adults.summary) %>%
  mutate(reveal_step = (as.integer(measure) - 1L) * 4L +
           (as.integer(condition) - 1L) * 2L + if_else(population == "Adults", 1L, 2L))
stopifnot(nrow(df.single.summary) == 40L, all(df.single.adults.summary$n == 16L))
write_csv(select(df.single.summary, population, age_group, age, condition, measure, n, mean, lower, upper),
          file.path(single_output, "single_cause_developmental_values.csv"))
kable(select(df.single.summary, population, age_group, condition, measure, n, mean, lower, upper), digits = 6,
      caption = "Every plotted child/adult mean and N (proportion units); CSV preserves full precision")

plot_single = function(summary, step = 16L) {
  visible = show_build(summary, step) %>%
    mutate(plot_x = x + unname(comparison_offsets[as.character(condition)]))
  ggplot(visible, aes(x = plot_x, y = mean, color = condition, fill = condition,
                     shape = condition, linetype = condition)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(0, .25, .75, 1), linetype = "dotted", color = "#E0E0E0", linewidth = .45) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed", color = "#888888", linewidth = .65) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 6.75, linetype = "dotted", color = "#C0C0C0", linewidth = .5) +
    geom_line(data = filter(visible, population == "Children"), aes(group = condition),
              linewidth = plot_line_width, show.legend = TRUE) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), linetype = "solid",
                   linewidth = ci_line_width, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_point(size = plot_point_size, stroke = .9, show.legend = TRUE) +
    facet_wrap(~ measure, ncol = 2, drop = FALSE, axes = "all_x", axis.labels = "all_x") +
    scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = comparison_colors, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Intentional = comparison_colors[["Intentional"]], Accidental = "white"),
                      limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = condition_shapes, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_linetype_manual(name = NULL, values = condition_lines, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(single_child_ages, single_adult_position),
                       labels = c(as.character(single_child_ages), "Adult"),
                       limits = c(2.6, single_adult_position + .5), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, .25), labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%"),
                       limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(add = .035)) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = '\"Yes\" Responses (%)') + talk_theme(study2_text_size)
}
p.single.full = plot_single(df.single.summary)
save_talk(p.single.full, file.path(single_output, "single_cause_yes_responses_full"), study2_width, study2_height)
p.single.builds = save_builds(df.single.summary, plot_single, single_output,
                              study2_width, study2_height, single_build_names)
p.single.full
```

Build 00 is the blank scaffold. Each measure adds Intentional adults, then
Intentional children, then Accidental adults, then Accidental children.
Caused occupies 01–04, Lexical 05–08, Fault 09–12 and Punish 13–16.
Axes, legends, panels and whitespace are fixed across all 17 builds;
Build 16 is the full figure.

## Secondary summary: children pooled across ages 3–6

Pool the same participant means within condition and measure, without giving
equal weight to age groups. This is an unadjusted summary of the supplied
child sample (50 Intentional, 46 Accidental). Each point's interval bootstraps
participants, not trials. The thin connectors join condition means within each
measure only; conditions are between participants, not within-child pairs.

```{r single-collapsed-summary}
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 5L)
df.single.collapsed = df.single.means %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order)) %>%
  arrange(measure, condition, participant) %>% group_by(measure, condition) %>%
  summarise(summary = list(bootstrap_mean(yes_mean)), .groups = "drop") %>% unnest_wider(summary) %>%
  mutate(plot_x = as.numeric(measure) + unname(intention_offsets[as.character(condition)]))
write_csv(select(df.single.collapsed, measure, condition, n, mean, lower, upper),
          file.path(single_output, "single_cause_intentionality_summary_values.csv"))
kable(select(df.single.collapsed, measure, condition, n, mean, lower, upper), digits = 6,
      caption = "Pooled child Yes proportions and pointwise 95% intervals")
df.single.pairs = df.single.collapsed %>% select(measure, condition, mean, plot_x) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(mean, plot_x))
p.single.collapsed = ggplot(df.single.collapsed,
  aes(x = plot_x, y = mean, color = condition, fill = condition, shape = condition)) +
  geom_segment(data = df.single.pairs,
                aes(x = plot_x_Intentional, xend = plot_x_Accidental,
                    y = mean_Intentional, yend = mean_Accidental),
                inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "#A0A0A0", linewidth = .6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = .055,
                linewidth = .55, alpha = .55, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 4.3, stroke = 1, show.legend = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = comparison_colors, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Intentional = comparison_colors[["Intentional"]], Accidental = "white"),
                    limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = condition_shapes, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(measure_order), labels = measure_order,
                     limits = c(.5, 4.5), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1, .25), labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%"),
                     limits = c(0, 1), expand = expansion(add = .035)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Proportion yes (%)") + talk_theme(intention_text_size)
save_talk(p.single.collapsed, file.path(single_output, "single_cause_intentionality_summary"),
          intention_width, intention_height)
p.single.collapsed
```

# Cross-study synthesis: where intention changes judgments

This comparison uses **children aged 3–6 in both studies**: Single Cause
(50 Intentional, 46 Accidental) and Study 2 (107 Intentional, 116 Accidental).
Matching the available age range avoids comparing Single Cause ages 3–6 with
Study 2 ages 3–9. Adults remain separate endpoints in the developmental plots;
Study 1 is absent because it has no intentionality manipulation.

For each measure and causal structure, the plotted quantity is
**100 × (mean Intentional Yes − mean Accidental Yes)**, in percentage points.
Each child's Yes/No responses are first averaged across available scenarios.
We then weight participants equally within study and condition, not age groups
equally. These are unadjusted descriptive effects for the matched age range;
the studies still have different age compositions and cohorts. The plot does
not isolate causal structure from all other between-study differences.

The two conditions contain different participants, so no individual child
has an Intentional-minus-Accidental score. For each bootstrap replicate we
sample participants independently within each study and condition, preserving
all measures and both Study 2 roles together on each sampled participant row.
We subtract the two bootstrapped condition means, using 5,000 replicates and
their 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles for the 95% interval. Thus both conditions'
uncertainty enters each interval; trial rows are never independently resampled.

```{r synthesis-summary}
df.synthesis.means = bind_rows(
  df.single.means %>% filter(age %in% synthesis_ages) %>%
    transmute(study = "Single Cause", structure = "Single Cause", participant, age,
              condition, measure, yes_mean),
  df.study2.means %>% filter(population == "Children", age %in% synthesis_ages) %>%
    transmute(study = "Study 2", structure = paste("Study 2", role), participant, age,
              condition, measure, yes_mean)) %>%
  mutate(structure = factor(structure, levels = synthesis_order),
         measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order))
stopifnot(!anyNA(df.synthesis.means$yes_mean),
          !anyDuplicated(df.synthesis.means[c("study", "participant", "condition", "structure", "measure")]))
df.synthesis.ns = df.synthesis.means %>% distinct(study, participant, age, condition) %>%
  count(study, condition, name = "n")
stopifnot(identical(df.synthesis.ns$n, c(50L, 46L, 107L, 116L)))
kable(df.synthesis.ns, caption = "Synthesis sample: children aged 3–6 only, equally weighted within condition")

# Wide rows keep each participant's four measures and (in Study 2) both roles together.
df.synthesis.wide = df.synthesis.means %>%
  mutate(score = paste(structure, measure, sep = "__")) %>%
  select(study, participant, condition, score, yes_mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = score, values_from = yes_mean) %>%
  arrange(study, condition, participant)
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 6L)
synthesis_intervals = list()
for (study_name in c("Single Cause", "Study 2")) {
  sample_rows = filter(df.synthesis.wide, study == study_name)
  score_columns = df.synthesis.means %>% filter(study == study_name) %>%
    transmute(score = paste(structure, measure, sep = "__")) %>% distinct() %>% pull(score)
  intentional = sample_rows %>% filter(condition == "Intentional") %>%
    select(all_of(score_columns)) %>% as.matrix()
  accidental = sample_rows %>% filter(condition == "Accidental") %>%
    select(all_of(score_columns)) %>% as.matrix()
  stopifnot(!anyNA(intentional), !anyNA(accidental))
  draws = replicate(bootstrap_replicates, {
    intentional_rows = sample.int(nrow(intentional), replace = TRUE)
    accidental_rows = sample.int(nrow(accidental), replace = TRUE)
    100 * (colMeans(intentional[intentional_rows, , drop = FALSE]) -
             colMeans(accidental[accidental_rows, , drop = FALSE]))
  })
  synthesis_intervals[[study_name]] = tibble(
    score = score_columns,
    lower_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .025),
    upper_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .975))
}
df.synthesis.intervals = bind_rows(synthesis_intervals) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(score, delim = "__", names = c("structure", "measure"))
df.synthesis.summary = df.synthesis.means %>% group_by(structure, measure, condition) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), yes = mean(yes_mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(n, yes)) %>%
  mutate(effect_pp = 100 * (yes_Intentional - yes_Accidental)) %>%
  left_join(df.synthesis.intervals, by = c("structure", "measure"), relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(population = "Children ages 3–6",
         structure = factor(structure, levels = synthesis_order),
         measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order)) %>%
  select(population, measure, structure, n_Intentional, n_Accidental,
         yes_Intentional, yes_Accidental, effect_pp, lower_pp, upper_pp) %>%
  arrange(measure, structure)
stopifnot(nrow(df.synthesis.summary) == 12L,
          all(is.finite(df.synthesis.summary$effect_pp)),
          all(df.synthesis.summary$lower_pp <= df.synthesis.summary$upper_pp))
write_csv(df.synthesis.summary,
          file.path(synthesis_output, "study2_singlecause_intention_effect_comparison_values.csv"))
kable(df.synthesis.summary, digits = 6,
      caption = "Exact plotted intention effects: source Yes proportions, Ns and percentage-point estimates/95% intervals")
```

## Grouped point-range figure

Single Cause uses gray squares, Study 2 Distal uses the existing red circles,
and Study 2 Proximal uses the existing blue triangles. Offsets separate the
three structures within each measure; there are no connecting lines. Zero
means equal Yes endorsement between conditions. The range contains every
point and interval end.

```{r synthesis-plot, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
df.synthesis.plot = df.synthesis.summary %>%
  mutate(plot_x = as.numeric(measure) + unname(synthesis_offsets[as.character(structure)]))
synthesis_y_lower = floor(min(0, df.synthesis.plot$lower_pp) / gap_y_step) * gap_y_step
synthesis_y_upper = ceiling(max(0, df.synthesis.plot$upper_pp) / gap_y_step) * gap_y_step
p.synthesis = ggplot(df.synthesis.plot, aes(x = plot_x, y = effect_pp, color = structure, shape = structure)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#777777", linewidth = .6) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower_pp, ymax = upper_pp), linewidth = ci_line_width, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 4.5, show.legend = TRUE) +
  scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = synthesis_colors, limits = synthesis_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = synthesis_shapes, limits = synthesis_order, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq_along(measure_order), labels = measure_order,
                     limits = c(.5, 4.5), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(synthesis_y_lower, synthesis_y_upper, gap_y_step),
                     labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), limits = c(synthesis_y_lower, synthesis_y_upper),
                     expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Effect of intention\n(percentage points)") + talk_theme(intention_text_size)
save_talk(p.synthesis, file.path(synthesis_output, "study2_singlecause_intention_effect_comparison"),
          intention_width, intention_height)
p.synthesis
```

The intervals are pointwise, descriptive participant bootstraps. Their overlap
or separation does not test whether effects differ across studies or measures.
In this matched-age sample, Single Cause has the largest positive point estimate
for Caused, Fault and Punish. Study 2 Distal is positive for all four measures,
with Lexical slightly larger than Punish. Study 2 Proximal is negative for all
four; its Lexical interval is below zero, so Proximal is not uniformly near zero.
Punish therefore does not uniquely dominate this synthesis. These patterns do
not establish a significant ordering of structures or measures.

# Developmental-stage synthesis figures

These **additional** figures show ordinary Yes-response proportions. They do
not replace the baseline-change, Study 2 role-gap, pooled Single Cause or
cross-study intention-effect figures above. None uses relative attribution.
Both Yes contributes 1 to each role and Neither contributes 0 to each role.

## Samples, stages and source datasets

**3–4** includes only children aged 3 or 4; **5–6** includes only ages 5 or 6.
Children aged 7–9 stay in the developmental figures but are not included in
these new stage summaries. **Adults** remain a separate category, never pooled
with children. Participants receive equal weights within study, stage and
condition; the individual ages within a stage do not receive equal weights.
Stages describe cross-sectional samples, not longitudinal change.

The same screened samples and selection rules used above are retained:

- Study 1 Baseline: [exp4 child snapshot](../../data/study1_baseline_causal_chains/children/exp4_raw_responses.csv)
  and [preregistered adult data](../../data/study1_baseline_causal_chains/adults/chains_baseline_full_run-responses.csv), N=100 adults.
- Study 2 Intentional/Accidental: [exp6 child snapshot](../../data/study2_intention_causal_chains/children/exp6_raw_responses.csv)
  and the selected [earlier adult pilot](../../data/study2_intention_causal_chains/adults/adult_pilot_rounds_unordered/exp2_new_pilot-responses.csv),
  N=20 Intentional and 21 Accidental adults. The main preregistered adult data remain missing.
- Single Cause: [exp7 child snapshot](../../data/single_cause/children/exp7_raw_responses.csv)
  and [all 32 recovered complete adults](../../data/single_cause/adults/single_cause_pilot1-responses.csv),
  N=16 in each condition. The historical N=30 subset remains unidentified.

Each participant's available Bike/Mirror responses are averaged **before**
group averaging. One missing scenario answer does not become No or discard
another role's answer: the available scenario supplies that participant mean.
If both scenarios are missing, that participant contributes no mean for that
particular measure/role. Tables report both eligible and contributing Ns.
The current samples have both scenarios for every plotted participant mean.

Intervals are the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles of 5,000 bootstrap means,
resampling participants within each displayed study/stage/condition/measure/role
cell. They are pointwise intervals for individual means, not intervals or tests
for the separation between endpoints. Thin connectors pair **group means**;
Intentional and Accidental are different participants. Distal and Proximal are
judgments made by the same participants within each chain condition. No trial
rows are treated as independent observations.

```{r developmental-stage-summaries}
stage_group = function(population, age) {
  factor(case_when(population == "Adults" ~ "Adults",
                   age %in% 3:4 ~ "3–4", age %in% 5:6 ~ "5–6"), levels = stage_order)
}
df.stage.means = bind_rows(
  df.study1.means, df.study2.means,
  df.single.means %>% mutate(study = "Single Cause", population = "Children", role = "Direct"),
  df.single.adults.means %>% mutate(study = "Single Cause", population = "Adults", age = NA_integer_, role = "Direct")) %>%
  mutate(stage = stage_group(population, age)) %>% filter(!is.na(stage)) %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Baseline", condition_order)))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.stage.means[c("study", "participant", "condition", "measure", "role")]),
          all(df.stage.means$scenarios_available == 2L))
df.stage.ns = df.stage.means %>% distinct(study, stage, condition, participant) %>%
  count(study, stage, condition, name = "n")
kable(df.stage.ns, caption = "Exact participants by source study, developmental stage and condition")

# Compute each group once; shared endpoints use identical estimates and intervals
# wherever they appear in the three synthesis figures.
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 8L)
df.stage.summary = df.stage.means %>%
  arrange(study, stage, condition, measure, role, participant) %>%
  group_by(study, population, stage, condition, measure, role) %>%
  summarise(eligible_n = n(), summary = list(bootstrap_mean(yes_mean)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest_wider(summary) %>%
  mutate(yes_pct = 100 * mean, lower_pct = 100 * lower, upper_pct = 100 * upper)
stopifnot(all(df.stage.summary$n == df.stage.summary$eligible_n),
          all(df.stage.summary$lower >= 0), all(df.stage.summary$upper <= 1))

# Reuse the established intention palette and filled-circle/open-triangle keys.
stage_condition_scales = function() {
  list(scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = comparison_colors, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE),
       scale_fill_manual(name = NULL, values = c(Intentional = comparison_colors[["Intentional"]], Accidental = "white"),
                         limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE),
       scale_shape_manual(name = NULL, values = condition_shapes, limits = condition_order, drop = FALSE))
}
percent_labels = function(x) paste0(100 * x, "%")
```

## Intention and causal role in punishment

For Single Cause and Chain: Distal, the condition varies the judged person's
own intention. For **Chain: Proximal**, it varies the **distal person's intention**,
not the proximal producer's own intention. That distinction is essential to
reading the three targets. The separate adult cohorts have the provenance and
sample limitations above; this is not an isolated causal-structure experiment.

```{r punishment-stage-table}
df.punishment.summary = df.stage.summary %>%
  filter(study %in% c("Single Cause", "Study 2"), measure == "Punish") %>%
  mutate(target = factor(if_else(study == "Single Cause", "Single Cause", paste0("Chain: ", role)),
                         levels = stage_target_order)) %>% arrange(stage, target, condition)
stopifnot(nrow(df.punishment.summary) == 18L)
write_csv(df.punishment.summary, file.path(synthesis_output, "punishment_causal_structure_intention_values.csv"))
kable(select(df.punishment.summary, stage, target, condition, eligible_n, n, yes_pct, lower_pct, upper_pct),
      digits = 6, caption = "Punishment: exact group means, Ns and 95% intervals (%); CSV retains full precision")
```

```{r punishment-stage-plot, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
df.punishment.pairs = df.punishment.plot %>% select(stage, target, condition, mean, plot_x) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(mean, plot_x))
p.punishment = ggplot(df.punishment.plot,
  aes(x = plot_x, y = mean, color = condition, fill = condition, shape = condition)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = .5, linetype = "dashed", color = "#B0B0B0", linewidth = .5) +
  geom_segment(data = df.punishment.pairs,
               aes(x = plot_x_Intentional, xend = plot_x_Accidental, y = mean_Intentional, yend = mean_Accidental),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "#A0A0A0", linewidth = .55) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), linewidth = .45, alpha = .65, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 3.8, stroke = .9) + stage_condition_scales() +

                     limits = c(.5, 3.5), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +

  labs(x = NULL, y = 'Punish: "Yes" Responses (%)') + talk_theme(stage_text_size) +
```

Baseline is Study 1; Intentional and Accidental are Study 2. Each connector
joins the Distal and Proximal group means at a single condition position.
There are no lines between Baseline, Intentional and Accidental. Existing

# Additional candidate synthesis plots

These six outputs are **additions**: each candidate has a main version without
intervals and a backup with pointwise 95% participant-bootstrap intervals.
Existing figures and builds keep their filenames, designs, data and availability.
Both versions of a candidate use the same table, positions, scales and legend;
only the interval layer differs. Every table below reports exactly the plotted
values, with full precision retained in its new CSV.

The samples and source datasets are those documented in the developmental-stage
section above. Ages **3 and 4 → 3–4**; ages **5 and 6 → 5–6**. Adults stay separate,
and ages 7–9 do not enter these grouped candidates. Study 1 adults are N=100;
Study 2 adults are the earlier pilot (N=20 Intentional, 21 Accidental);
Single Cause uses all 32 recovered adults (N=16 per condition). The historical
Single Cause N=30 exclusions and missing Study 2 main adult data remain unresolved.

Yes and No stay independent 1/0 endorsements for every role. Both Yes and
Neither remain valid responses. No relative-distal score enters these figures.
Available scenarios are averaged within participant before participants are
averaged within a group. Missing answers never become No, and no participant's
other valid judgments are discarded because one question is missing.

```{r candidate-synthesis-checks}
check_labels(df.stage.means$study, c("Study 1", "Study 2", "Single Cause"), "candidate source study")
stopifnot(all(df.stage.means$condition[df.stage.means$study == "Study 1"] == "Baseline"),
          all(df.stage.means$condition[df.stage.means$study != "Study 1"] %in% condition_order),
          setequal(as.character(df.stage.means$stage), stage_order),
          all(df.stage.means$population == "Adults" | df.stage.means$age %in% 3:6),
          !anyDuplicated(df.stage.means[c("study", "participant", "stage", "condition", "measure", "role")]),
          all(is.na(df.stage.means$yes_mean) | dplyr::between(df.stage.means$yes_mean, 0, 1)))
mean_available = function(values) {
  if (all(is.na(values))) NA_real_ else mean(values, na.rm = TRUE)
}
# Both candidate versions share a scale large enough for every point and interval.
# Differences of two binary-endorsement proportions have the range -100 to 100 pp.
candidate_difference_scale = function(limits = c(-100, 100)) {
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(limits[1], limits[2], 50), labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
                     limits = limits, expand = expansion(add = 3.5))
}
```

## Candidate 2: Caused versus Lexical role preference

For each participant × scenario × measure, subtract the Proximal binary answer
from the Distal binary answer. Then average the available **paired-scenario
differences within participant**, and finally average those participant means
within source study, stage, condition and measure. Both Yes and Neither yield
zero; Distal-only yields +1 and Proximal-only yields −1. Multiply by 100 to show
percentage points. A scenario missing either role cannot supply a paired
difference; other complete scenarios and other judgments remain available.
Participants with no complete pair for one measure are omitted only from that
measure's mean, with eligible/contributing Ns reported separately.

The bootstrap resamples each participant's paired-role mean, preserving the
within-person role pairing. It does not subtract separately bootstrapped role
means or calculate Distal/(Distal+Proximal). Lines connect experimental-context
group means, not repeated measurements of the same people across conditions or
studies. The new fixed Set1 measure palette is shared with Candidate 3.

```{r role-preference-candidate-means}
role_preference_means = function(responses) {
  check_response_rows(responses)
  responses %>%
    mutate(role = factor(role, levels = role_order)) %>%
    pivot_wider(id_cols = c(study, population, participant, age, condition, scenario, measure),
                 names_from = role, values_from = endorsed, names_expand = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(scenario_difference = Distal - Proximal) %>%
    group_by(study, population, participant, age, condition, measure) %>%
    summarise(paired_scenarios = sum(!is.na(scenario_difference)),
              role_difference = mean_available(scenario_difference), .groups = "drop")
}
df.role.preference.responses = bind_rows(
  df.study1.adults.responses, df.study1.children.responses,
  df.study2.adults.responses, df.study2.children.responses) %>%
  filter(measure %in% c("Caused", "Lexical"), population == "Adults" | age %in% 3:6)
check_labels(df.role.preference.responses$study, c("Study 1", "Study 2"), "role-preference study")
df.role.preference.means = role_preference_means(df.role.preference.responses) %>%
  mutate(stage = stage_group(population, age),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = c("Baseline", condition_order)),
         measure = factor(measure, levels = c("Caused", "Lexical")))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.role.preference.means[c("study", "participant", "condition", "measure")]),
          !anyNA(df.role.preference.means$stage),
          all(df.role.preference.means$paired_scenarios %in% 0:2),
          all(is.na(df.role.preference.means$role_difference) |
                dplyr::between(df.role.preference.means$role_difference, -1, 1)))
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 9L)
df.role.preference.summary = df.role.preference.means %>%
  arrange(study, stage, condition, measure, participant) %>%
  group_by(study, population, stage, condition, measure) %>%
  summarise(eligible_n = n(), summary = list(bootstrap_mean(role_difference)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest_wider(summary) %>%
  transmute(study, population, stage, condition, measure, eligible_n, n,
            mean_pp = 100 * mean, lower_pp = 100 * lower, upper_pp = 100 * upper) %>%
  arrange(stage, measure, condition)
stopifnot(nrow(df.role.preference.summary) == 18L,
          all(dplyr::between(df.role.preference.summary$mean_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(dplyr::between(df.role.preference.summary$lower_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(dplyr::between(df.role.preference.summary$upper_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(df.role.preference.summary$n <= df.role.preference.summary$eligible_n),
          nrow(count(df.role.preference.summary, stage, condition, measure)) == 18L)
```

```{r role-preference-candidate-plot, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}
p.role.preference = plot_role_preference()

save_talk(p.role.preference.ci, file.path(synthesis_output, "caused_lexical_role_preference_with_ci"), 16, 9)
```

## Candidate 3: Single Cause sensitivity to intention across judgments

The effect is **100 × (Intentional group mean Yes − Accidental group mean Yes)**.
The inputs are scenario-averaged participant means from Single Cause only.
The two conditions contain different people, so the difference is between group
means, not a within-person intention difference. Adults are the same working
N=32 sample; these plots do not identify the historical N=30 exclusions.

For each stage, independently resample whole Intentional and Accidental
participants 5,000 times and subtract the sampled group means. All four
judgments stay together on each participant's sampled row. A missing measure
mean is ignored only for that measure, not for a participant's other valid
judgments. The table gives eligible and contributing Ns separately for the two
conditions, plus source means and the resulting difference. The backup uses
percentile intervals from the differences, including uncertainty in both groups.
Lines describe separate cross-sectional age samples, not within-person change.
Small fixed horizontal offsets separate overlapping measure points.

```{r single-sensitivity-candidate-means}
df.single.sensitivity.means = df.stage.means %>% filter(study == "Single Cause")
check_labels(df.single.sensitivity.means$condition, condition_order, "Single Cause sensitivity condition")
stopifnot(setequal(as.character(df.single.sensitivity.means$stage), stage_order),
          !anyDuplicated(df.single.sensitivity.means[c("participant", "stage", "condition", "measure")]))
df.single.sensitivity.wide = df.single.sensitivity.means %>%
  select(stage, condition, participant, measure, yes_mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = measure, values_from = yes_mean) %>% arrange(stage, condition, participant)
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 10L)
sensitivity_intervals = list()
for (stage_name in stage_order) {
  rows = filter(df.single.sensitivity.wide, stage == stage_name)
  intentional = rows %>% filter(condition == "Intentional") %>% select(all_of(measure_order)) %>% as.matrix()
  accidental = rows %>% filter(condition == "Accidental") %>% select(all_of(measure_order)) %>% as.matrix()
  stopifnot(nrow(intentional) > 0L, nrow(accidental) > 0L)
  draws = replicate(bootstrap_replicates, {
    i = sample.int(nrow(intentional), replace = TRUE)
    a = sample.int(nrow(accidental), replace = TRUE)
    100 * (apply(intentional[i, , drop = FALSE], 2, mean_available) -
             apply(accidental[a, , drop = FALSE], 2, mean_available))
  })
  sensitivity_intervals[[stage_name]] = tibble(stage = stage_name, measure = measure_order,
    lower_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .975, na.rm = TRUE))
}
df.single.sensitivity.summary = df.single.sensitivity.means %>%
  group_by(stage, condition, measure) %>%
  summarise(eligible_n = n(), n = sum(!is.na(yes_mean)), yes_mean = mean_available(yes_mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(eligible_n, n, yes_mean)) %>%
  mutate(mean_pp = 100 * (yes_mean_Intentional - yes_mean_Accidental)) %>%
  left_join(bind_rows(sensitivity_intervals), by = c("stage", "measure"), relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(study = "Single Cause", contrast = "Intentional minus Accidental",
         stage = factor(stage, levels = stage_order), measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order)) %>%
  select(study, stage, contrast, measure, eligible_n_Intentional, eligible_n_Accidental,
         n_Intentional, n_Accidental, yes_mean_Intentional, yes_mean_Accidental, mean_pp, lower_pp, upper_pp) %>%
  arrange(stage, measure)
stopifnot(nrow(df.single.sensitivity.summary) == 12L,
          !anyDuplicated(df.single.sensitivity.summary[c("stage", "measure")]),
          all(df.single.sensitivity.summary$n_Intentional > 0L), all(df.single.sensitivity.summary$n_Accidental > 0L),
          all(dplyr::between(df.single.sensitivity.summary$mean_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(dplyr::between(df.single.sensitivity.summary$lower_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(dplyr::between(df.single.sensitivity.summary$upper_pp, -100, 100)))
```

```{r single-sensitivity-candidate-plot, fig.width=16, fig.height=9}

  mutate(plot_x = as.numeric(stage) + unname(sensitivity_offsets[as.character(measure)]))
plot_single_sensitivity = function(with_ci = FALSE) {
  p = ggplot(df.single.sensitivity.plot,
              aes(x = plot_x, y = mean_pp, color = measure, shape = measure, group = measure)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#666666", linewidth = .75) +
    geom_line(linewidth = .8)
  if (with_ci) {

  }
  p + geom_point(size = 4.5) +
    scale_color_manual(name = NULL, values = measure_colors, limits = measure_order, drop = FALSE) +

    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = stage_order, limits = c(.65, 3.35), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    candidate_difference_scale(limits = c(-50, 100)) +

}
stopifnot(all(df.single.sensitivity.summary$lower_pp >= -50),
          all(df.single.sensitivity.summary$upper_pp <= 100))

p.single.sensitivity.ci = plot_single_sensitivity(with_ci = TRUE)
save_talk(p.single.sensitivity, file.path(synthesis_output, "single_cause_intention_sensitivity"), 16, 9)
save_talk(p.single.sensitivity.ci, file.path(synthesis_output, "single_cause_intention_sensitivity_with_ci"), 16, 9)
p.single.sensitivity
```

# Presentation V2 — development from left to right

These are additional presentation versions of the three candidates above. The
participant-first calculations, inclusion rules, age groups, source datasets,
weights, adult samples and bootstrap intervals are unchanged. Each V2 table is
checked against its earlier candidate CSV. No old figure or build is replaced.
All new files go to `../../figures/study_comparison/presentation_v2/`.

The visual reference is cookie-task's final Study 1 victim figure and Builds
00–04 in `current/figures/study1/change_from_45_final/`. Before implementing
this section, both those PDFs and the actual `conference_theme()`,
`plot_change_from_45_v2()`, `plot_change_from_45_final()` and
`plot_final_developmental_change()` helpers in its `cookie_allocation.Rmd`
were inspected. The resolved final theme, not an earlier prototype, supplies
the constants below. This Rmd has no runtime dependency on cookie-task.

## Shared presentation settings and helper

The reference scales its 12-inch conference typography by **22/12** for the
22 × 8.5-inch canvas. This gives 44 pt base/tick/panel text, 47⅔ pt long axis
titles, and 42⅙ pt legends. Panels have equal flexible widths with 1⅚ cm gaps.
The childhood band ends exactly at the second child tick; Adults have the same
one-unit spacing as the two childhood groups. No extra gap or opacity reduction
is introduced. The reference's final line figure uses no gtable edits; its
separate bar helper's .45-inch top spacer is not used here.

Long axis titles are wrapped over two lines to retain the reference's large
font. V2 C keeps the existing measure colors and geometric shapes, using their
fillable equivalents so all marks can have the reference's black outlines.
The complete legend stays visible even when every data mark has alpha zero.

```{r presentation-v2-settings}
talk_v2 = list(
  width = 22, height = 8.5, dpi = png_dpi, text_scale = 22 / 12,
  base_size = 11 * 22 / 12, tick_size = 24 * 22 / 12,
  panel_title_size = 24 * 22 / 12, axis_title_size = 26 * 22 / 12,
  legend_size = 23 * 22 / 12, panel_spacing_cm = 22 / 12,
  legend_key_cm = .85 * 22 / 12,
  line_width = 2.1, point_size = 6.2, point_stroke = 1.15,
  reference_width = 1, axis_width = .65, ci_width = .85,
  childhood_fill = "#F3F3F3", childhood_end = 2, x_padding = .25)
presentation_v2_output = file.path(synthesis_output, "presentation_v2")
dir.create(presentation_v2_output, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Intentionally matched to cookie-task's FINAL conference-figure design:
# conference_theme(long_axis_title = TRUE, figure_width = 22), followed by
# plot_final_developmental_change()'s strip size, right margin and panel spacing.
theme_causal_verbs_talk = function() {
  s = talk_v2$text_scale
  theme_classic(base_family = "", base_size = talk_v2$base_size,
                base_line_size = .5, base_rect_size = .5) +
    theme(text = element_text(size = talk_v2$tick_size),
          axis.text = element_text(size = talk_v2$tick_size, color = "black"),
          axis.title = element_text(size = talk_v2$axis_title_size),
          strip.text = element_text(size = talk_v2$panel_title_size),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          axis.line = element_line(linewidth = talk_v2$axis_width),
          axis.ticks = element_line(linewidth = talk_v2$axis_width),
          panel.spacing = grid::unit(talk_v2$panel_spacing_cm, "cm"),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.justification = "center", legend.box.just = "center",
          legend.text = element_text(size = talk_v2$legend_size),
          legend.key.size = grid::unit(talk_v2$legend_key_cm, "cm"),
          plot.margin = margin(5, 14, 12, 12) * s + margin(r = talk_v2$tick_size / 2))
}

talk_v2_conditions = list(
  order = condition_order, colors = comparison_colors,
  fills = c(Intentional = comparison_colors[["Intentional"]], Accidental = NA),
  shapes = condition_shapes, lines = condition_lines)
talk_v2_contexts = list(
  order = c("Baseline", condition_order),
  colors = c(Baseline = "#666666", comparison_colors),
  fills = c(Baseline = "#666666", Intentional = comparison_colors[["Intentional"]], Accidental = NA),
  shapes = c(Baseline = 22, condition_shapes),
  lines = c(Baseline = "dotted", condition_lines))
talk_v2_measures = list(
  order = measure_order, colors = measure_colors, fills = measure_colors,
  shapes = c(Caused = 21, Lexical = 24, Fault = 22, Punish = 23),
  lines = setNames(rep("solid", 4), measure_order))
```

Every plot uses the same helper. Build visibility is encoded as alpha, leaving
all panel levels, scales, legends and positions fixed. A connecting segment
appears only when **both** its endpoints have been revealed. Main builds never
contain an interval layer. CI backups use the same stored intervals and are
saved separately; their ranges expand only when necessary to show every bound.

```{r presentation-v2-helper}
plot_causal_verbs_talk = function(values, panel_order, style, y_limits, y_breaks,
                                  y_label, reference, step, with_ci = FALSE, x_offsets = NULL,
                                  mark_settings = talk_v2) {
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(values[c("panel", "series", "stage")]),
            setequal(as.character(values$stage), stage_order),
            all(values$series %in% style$order), all(values$panel %in% panel_order),
            all(dplyr::between(values$mean, y_limits[1], y_limits[2])))
  if (with_ci) stopifnot(all(values$lower >= y_limits[1]), all(values$upper <= y_limits[2]))
  points = values %>%
    mutate(panel = factor(panel, levels = panel_order),
           series = factor(series, levels = style$order),
           x = match(as.character(stage), stage_order), visible = as.numeric(reveal_step <= step))
  x_limits = c(1, 3)
  x_expansion = expansion(add = talk_v2$x_padding)
  band_end = talk_v2$childhood_end
  if (!is.null(x_offsets)) {
    # Optional fixed offsets separate overlapping measures in the NEW one-panel
    # family. Existing figures take the unchanged no-offset path.
    stopifnot(setequal(names(x_offsets), style$order), all(abs(x_offsets) < talk_v2$x_padding))
    points = points %>% mutate(x = x + unname(x_offsets[as.character(series)]))
    x_limits = c(1 - talk_v2$x_padding, 3 + talk_v2$x_padding)
    x_expansion = expansion(mult = 0)
    band_end = talk_v2$childhood_end + max(x_offsets)
  }
  segments = points %>% arrange(panel, series, x) %>% group_by(panel, series) %>%
    mutate(end_x = lead(x), end_y = lead(mean), end_step = lead(reveal_step)) %>% ungroup() %>%
    filter(!is.na(end_x)) %>% mutate(visible = as.numeric(pmax(reveal_step, end_step) <= step))
  p = ggplot(points, aes(x = x, y = mean, group = series)) +
    annotate("rect", xmin = -Inf, xmax = band_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
             fill = talk_v2$childhood_fill, color = NA) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = reference, color = "black", linetype = "dashed",
               linewidth = talk_v2$reference_width) +
    geom_segment(data = segments,
                 aes(xend = end_x, yend = end_y, color = series, linetype = series, alpha = visible),
                 linewidth = mark_settings$line_width, show.legend = TRUE)
  if (with_ci) {
    p = p + geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, color = series, alpha = visible),
                            linewidth = talk_v2$ci_width, show.legend = FALSE)
  }
  p + geom_point(aes(fill = series, shape = series, alpha = visible),
                 size = mark_settings$point_size, color = "black", stroke = mark_settings$point_stroke,
                 show.legend = TRUE) +
    facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_alpha_identity(guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(NULL, values = style$colors, limits = style$order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(NULL, values = style$fills, limits = style$order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_shape_manual(NULL, values = style$shapes, limits = style$order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_linetype_manual(NULL, values = style$lines, limits = style$order, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = stage_order, limits = x_limits,
                       expand = x_expansion) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = y_limits, breaks = y_breaks,
                       labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = y_label) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(nrow = 1, override.aes = list(alpha = 1)),
           fill = guide_legend(nrow = 1), shape = guide_legend(nrow = 1), linetype = guide_legend(nrow = 1)) +
    theme_causal_verbs_talk()
}

save_presentation_v2 = function(plot, filename, width = talk_v2$width, height = talk_v2$height) {
  ggsave(paste0(filename, ".pdf"), plot = plot, width = width, height = height,
         device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white")
  ggsave(paste0(filename, ".png"), plot = plot, width = width, height = height,
         device = ragg::agg_png, dpi = talk_v2$dpi, bg = "white")
}

save_presentation_v2_family = function(plot_function, stem, build_folder, build_names,
                                        width = talk_v2$width, height = talk_v2$height) {
  directory = file.path(presentation_v2_output, "builds", build_folder)
  dir.create(directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  final_step = length(build_names) - 1L
  main = plot_function(final_step)
  backup = plot_function(final_step, with_ci = TRUE)
  filename = file.path(presentation_v2_output, stem)
  save_presentation_v2(main, filename, width, height)
  save_presentation_v2(backup, paste0(filename, "_with_ci"), width, height)
  builds = lapply(0:final_step, function(step) {
    plot = plot_function(step)
    build_filename = file.path(directory, build_names[step + 1L])
    if (step == final_step) {
      stopifnot(identical(ggplot_build(plot)$data, ggplot_build(main)$data))
      # The last reveal is the full figure, including identical exported bytes.
      for (extension in c(".pdf", ".png")) {
        stopifnot(file.copy(paste0(filename, extension), paste0(build_filename, extension), overwrite = TRUE))
      }
    } else save_presentation_v2(plot, build_filename, width, height)
    plot
  })
  list(main = main, backup = backup, builds = builds)
}
```

## V2 numerical identity and fixed-build checks

These files repeat the earlier candidate tables exactly, retaining their means,
Ns and 95% intervals. They are included beside the V2 figures for convenience;
the Rmd does not rerun scoring or bootstrapping for the redesign.

```{r presentation-v2-validation}
v2_tables = list(
  punishment_causal_structure = df.punishment.horizontal.values,
  caused_lexical_role_preference = df.role.preference.summary,
  single_cause_intention_sensitivity = df.single.sensitivity.summary)
v2_source_stems = c("punishment_causal_structure_horizontal", "caused_lexical_role_preference", "single_cause_intention_sensitivity")
for (i in seq_along(v2_tables)) {
  destination = file.path(presentation_v2_output, paste0(names(v2_tables)[i], "_talk_v2_values.csv"))
  source = file.path(synthesis_output, paste0(v2_source_stems[i], "_values.csv"))
  original = read_csv(source, show_col_types = FALSE)
  stopifnot(identical(names(original), names(v2_tables[[i]])))
  for (column in names(original)) {
    value = v2_tables[[i]][[column]]
    if (is.factor(value)) value = as.character(value)
    same_value = all.equal(unname(value), unname(original[[column]]), tolerance = 1e-12)
    if (!isTRUE(same_value)) stop("V2 numerical mismatch in ", names(v2_tables)[i], ": ", column,
                                 " — ", paste(same_value, collapse = "; "))
  }
  # Keep the original full-precision CSV bytes rather than round-trip its decimals.
  stopifnot(file.copy(source, destination, overwrite = TRUE),
            identical(readLines(source), readLines(destination)))
}
# Check all visibility transitions while retaining identical physical geometry.
check_presentation_builds = function(family, expected_points) {
  full_built = ggplot_build(family$main)
  full_grob = ggplotGrob(family$main)
  counts = integer(length(family$builds))
  for (i in seq_along(family$builds)) {
    plot = family$builds[[i]]
    built = ggplot_build(plot)
    grob = ggplotGrob(plot)
    stopifnot(identical(built$layout$layout, full_built$layout$layout),
              identical(grob$layout, full_grob$layout),
              isTRUE(all.equal(grid::convertWidth(grob$widths, "cm", valueOnly = TRUE),
                               grid::convertWidth(full_grob$widths, "cm", valueOnly = TRUE))),
              isTRUE(all.equal(grid::convertHeight(grob$heights, "cm", valueOnly = TRUE),
                               grid::convertHeight(full_grob$heights, "cm", valueOnly = TRUE))))
    for (panel in seq_along(built$layout$panel_params)) {
      stopifnot(identical(built$layout$panel_params[[panel]]$x.range, full_built$layout$panel_params[[panel]]$x.range),
                identical(built$layout$panel_params[[panel]]$y.range, full_built$layout$panel_params[[panel]]$y.range))
    }
    for (layer in seq_along(built$data)) {
      a = built$data[[layer]]
      b = full_built$data[[layer]]
      stopifnot(identical(a[setdiff(names(a), "alpha")], b[setdiff(names(b), "alpha")]))
      if ("alpha" %in% names(a) && !all(is.na(a$alpha))) {
        stopifnot(all(a$alpha %in% c(0, 1)))
        if (i > 1) stopifnot(all(a$alpha >= ggplot_build(family$builds[[i - 1]])$data[[layer]]$alpha))
      }
    }
    point_layer = which(vapply(plot$layers, function(x) inherits(x$geom, "GeomPoint"), logical(1)))
    counts[i] = sum(built$data[[point_layer]]$alpha == 1)
    stopifnot(!any(vapply(plot$layers, function(x) inherits(x$geom, "GeomLinerange"), logical(1))))
  }
  stopifnot(identical(counts, expected_points),
            identical(ggplot_build(family$builds[[length(family$builds)]])$data, full_built$data))
  TRUE
}
stopifnot(check_presentation_builds(p.v2.punishment, c(0L, 6L, 12L, 18L)),
          check_presentation_builds(p.v2.preference, c(0L, 4L, 8L, 12L, 18L)),
          check_presentation_builds(p.v2.sensitivity, c(0L, 2L, 4L, 6L, 8L, 12L)))
kable(tibble(figure = names(v2_tables), points = c(18, 18, 12), builds = c(4, 5, 6),
             numerical_values_unchanged = TRUE, fixed_build_geometry = TRUE, final_build_equals_full = TRUE))
```

# Additional presentation syntheses — all judgments and one-panel sensitivity

These two new families leave every previous figure and build unchanged,
including punishment V2, the focused two-panel Caused/Lexical figure and the
four-panel Single Cause sensitivity figure. They reuse the exact final
cookie-task presentation settings and shared plotting/build helpers above.
The reference helper chain and its final Study 1 victim builds were rechecked
before this addition; no cookie-task files or analysis choices are changed.

## Four judgments: developmental Distal-minus-Proximal role preference

Use the same `role_preference_means()` helper for all four judgments: subtract
binary Proximal from binary Distal **within scenario**, average available paired
scenarios within participant, then average participant contrasts within
study/stage/condition. Both/Neither give zero. A missing role affects only its
scenario's contrast; other valid scenarios and judgments remain usable.

Caused/Lexical reuse their existing means and confidence intervals exactly.
Only the newly displayed Fault/Punish contrasts require additional intervals.
They use the unchanged 5,000-draw participant-bootstrap percentile procedure,
with a separate fixed seed (`bootstrap_seed + 11`) so adding measures does not
alter earlier Monte Carlo intervals. Inclusion, repeats, coding, age groups,
weights and adult samples remain as documented above. Study 2 adults remain
the earlier pilot; the missing main adult data and handoff gaps stay unresolved.

```{r role-preference-all-measures-summary}
df.role.preference.all.responses = bind_rows(
  df.study1.adults.responses, df.study1.children.responses,
  df.study2.adults.responses, df.study2.children.responses) %>%
  filter(population == "Adults" | age %in% 3:6)
check_labels(df.role.preference.all.responses$study, c("Study 1", "Study 2"), "all-measure source study")
check_labels(df.role.preference.all.responses$measure, measure_order, "all-measure judgment")
df.role.preference.all.means = role_preference_means(df.role.preference.all.responses) %>%
  mutate(stage = stage_group(population, age),
         condition = factor(condition, levels = talk_v2_contexts$order),
         measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order))
stopifnot(!anyNA(df.role.preference.all.means$stage), !anyNA(df.role.preference.all.means$condition),
          !anyDuplicated(df.role.preference.all.means[c("study", "participant", "condition", "measure")]),
          setequal(as.character(df.role.preference.all.means$stage), stage_order),
          all(df.role.preference.all.means$paired_scenarios %in% 0:2))
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 11L)
df.role.preference.additional = df.role.preference.all.means %>%
  filter(measure %in% c("Fault", "Punish")) %>%
  arrange(study, stage, condition, measure, participant) %>%
  group_by(study, population, stage, condition, measure) %>%
  summarise(eligible_n = n(), summary = list(bootstrap_mean(role_difference)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  unnest_wider(summary) %>%
  transmute(study, population, stage, condition, measure, eligible_n, n,
            mean_pp = 100 * mean, lower_pp = 100 * lower, upper_pp = 100 * upper)
df.role.preference.all.summary = bind_rows(
  mutate(df.role.preference.summary, measure = as.character(measure)),
  mutate(df.role.preference.additional, measure = as.character(measure))) %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order)) %>% arrange(stage, measure, condition)
stopifnot(nrow(df.role.preference.all.summary) == 36L,
          !anyDuplicated(df.role.preference.all.summary[c("stage", "condition", "measure")]),
          all(dplyr::between(df.role.preference.all.summary$mean_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(dplyr::between(df.role.preference.all.summary$lower_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(dplyr::between(df.role.preference.all.summary$upper_pp, -100, 100)))
# These snapshots contain complete scenario pairs. Therefore the paired contrast
# must also equal the difference of the already validated role-specific means.
stopifnot(all(df.role.preference.all.means$paired_scenarios == 2L))
df.role.preference.existing_check = df.stage.summary %>%
  filter(study %in% c("Study 1", "Study 2")) %>%
  select(study, stage, condition, measure, role, mean, n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = role, values_from = c(mean, n)) %>%
  mutate(expected_pp = 100 * (mean_Distal - mean_Proximal))
df.role.preference.all.check = df.role.preference.all.summary %>%
  left_join(df.role.preference.existing_check, by = c("study", "stage", "condition", "measure"),
            relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(nrow(df.role.preference.all.check) == 36L,
          all(abs(df.role.preference.all.check$mean_pp - df.role.preference.all.check$expected_pp) < 1e-10),
          all(df.role.preference.all.check$n == df.role.preference.all.check$n_Distal),
          all(df.role.preference.all.check$n == df.role.preference.all.check$n_Proximal))
shared = filter(df.role.preference.all.summary, measure %in% c("Caused", "Lexical"))
for (column in names(df.role.preference.summary)) {
  old = df.role.preference.summary[[column]]
  new = shared[[column]]
  if (is.factor(old)) old = as.character(old)
  if (is.factor(new)) new = as.character(new)
  stopifnot(identical(unname(old), unname(new)))
}
# Derive a clean symmetric scale from the data, allowing five points of padding
# where the theoretical -100..100 range permits it.
role_all_main_limit = min(100, ceiling((max(abs(df.role.preference.all.summary$mean_pp)) + 5) / 10) * 10)
role_all_ci_limit = max(role_all_main_limit,
  ceiling(max(abs(c(df.role.preference.all.summary$lower_pp, df.role.preference.all.summary$upper_pp))) / 10) * 10)
```

The observed means range from `r round(min(df.role.preference.all.summary$mean_pp), 3)`
to `r round(max(df.role.preference.all.summary$mean_pp), 3)` percentage points.
The data-derived symmetric main range is therefore ±`r role_all_main_limit`%,
with five major ticks. It is not inherited from a ±100% default. The separate
CI backup shows every bound without clipping. Positive values favor Distal;
negative values favor Proximal. Context colors/shapes/line types match the
existing two-panel figure exactly.

```{r role-preference-all-measures-plot, fig.width=22, fig.height=8.5}
# Reveal Accidental before Intentional in this all-measure build family only.
role_all_reveal_order = c("Baseline", "Accidental", "Intentional")
df.role.preference.all.plot = df.role.preference.all.summary %>%
  transmute(panel = as.character(measure), series = as.character(condition), stage,
            mean = mean_pp, lower = lower_pp, upper = upper_pp,
            reveal_step = if_else(stage == "Adults", 4L, match(condition, role_all_reveal_order)))
plot_role_preference_all = function(step = 4L, with_ci = FALSE) {
  limit = if (with_ci) role_all_ci_limit else role_all_main_limit
  plot_causal_verbs_talk(df.role.preference.all.plot, measure_order, talk_v2_contexts,
                         c(-limit, limit), seq(-limit, limit, length.out = 5),
                         "Distal − Proximal\nendorsement (%)", 0, step, with_ci)
}
p.role.preference.all = save_presentation_v2_family(
  plot_role_preference_all, "role_preference_all_measures_talk_v2", "role_preference_all_measures",
  c("build00_blank", "build01_baseline_childhood", "build02_add_accidental_childhood",
    "build03_add_intentional_childhood", "build04_add_adults_full"))
p.role.preference.all$main
p.role.preference.all$backup
p.role.preference.all$builds[[1]]
```

```{r role-preference-all-measures-table}
write_csv(df.role.preference.all.summary,
          file.path(presentation_v2_output, "role_preference_all_measures_talk_v2_values.csv"))
kable(select(df.role.preference.all.summary, study, stage, condition, measure, n, mean_pp, lower_pp, upper_pp),
      digits = 4, caption = "All judgments: paired Distal-minus-Proximal mean and 95% CI (pp); participant N; CSV retains full precision")
```

## Single Cause: one-panel comparison of intention sensitivity

This additional, preferred talk candidate overlays the four judgments in one
panel. It reuses **all 12 existing Single Cause estimates and intervals**;
no new scoring, resampling or participant selection occurs. Colors and outlined
shapes represent measures, with solid lines for all four. The prior four-panel
V2 figure remains available as a separate presentation option.

Start from the observed means with five points of padding, rounded outward to
multiples of 25. Expand that range only as needed for the existing interval
bounds, then use the **same axes for the main, all builds and CI backup**.
Main builds contain no intervals. Small fixed measure offsets separate nearby
markers and their CI bars without changing any y-value. The broad childhood
band includes both child groups and ends before Adults.

```{r single-sensitivity-onepanel-plot, fig.width=22, fig.height=8.5}
df.single.onepanel = df.v2.sensitivity %>% mutate(panel = "Single Cause")
single_onepanel_main_limits = c(
  floor((min(df.single.onepanel$mean) - 5) / 25) * 25,
  ceiling((max(df.single.onepanel$mean) + 5) / 25) * 25)
single_onepanel_ci_limits = c(
  min(single_onepanel_main_limits[1], floor(min(df.single.onepanel$lower) / 5) * 5),
  max(single_onepanel_main_limits[2], ceiling(max(df.single.onepanel$upper) / 5) * 5))
single_onepanel_offsets = c(Caused = -.045, Lexical = -.015, Fault = .015, Punish = .045)
plot_single_sensitivity_onepanel = function(step = 5L, with_ci = FALSE, mark_settings = talk_v2) {
  plot_causal_verbs_talk(df.single.onepanel, "Single Cause", talk_v2_measures,
                         single_onepanel_ci_limits,
                         seq(single_onepanel_main_limits[1], single_onepanel_main_limits[2], 25),
                         "Intentional −\nAccidental (%)", 0, step, with_ci,
                         x_offsets = single_onepanel_offsets, mark_settings = mark_settings)
}
p.single.onepanel = save_presentation_v2_family(
  plot_single_sensitivity_onepanel, "single_cause_intention_sensitivity_onepanel_talk_v3",
  "single_cause_intention_sensitivity_onepanel",
  c("build00_blank", "build01_caused_childhood", "build02_add_lexical_childhood",
    "build03_add_fault_childhood", "build04_add_punish_childhood", "build05_add_adults_full"))
p.single.onepanel$main
p.single.onepanel$backup
p.single.onepanel$builds[[1]]
```

Observed Single Cause sensitivity ranges from
`r round(min(df.single.onepanel$mean), 3)` to `r round(max(df.single.onepanel$mean), 3)`
percentage points. Both main and backup use a `r single_onepanel_ci_limits[1]`%
to `r single_onepanel_ci_limits[2]`% range: the existing −25.320513 lower CI
bound requires the small extension below the −25% major tick. There is no
geometry shift when swapping main and backup.

```{r single-sensitivity-onepanel-table}
onepanel_source = file.path(presentation_v2_output, "single_cause_intention_sensitivity_talk_v2_values.csv")
onepanel_destination = file.path(presentation_v2_output, "single_cause_intention_sensitivity_onepanel_talk_v3_values.csv")
stopifnot(file.copy(onepanel_source, onepanel_destination, overwrite = TRUE),
          identical(readLines(onepanel_source), readLines(onepanel_destination)),
          identical(df.single.onepanel$mean, df.v2.sensitivity$mean),
          identical(df.single.onepanel$lower, df.v2.sensitivity$lower),

kable(select(df.single.sensitivity.summary, stage, measure, n_Intentional, n_Accidental, mean_pp, lower_pp, upper_pp),
      digits = 4, caption = "Single Cause: unchanged Intentional-minus-Accidental mean and 95% CI (pp); participant Ns")
stopifnot(check_presentation_builds(p.role.preference.all, c(0L, 8L, 16L, 24L, 36L)),
          check_presentation_builds(p.single.onepanel, c(0L, 2L, 4L, 6L, 8L, 12L)))
```

## Single Cause V4: compact canvas and stronger marks

V4 changes only the one-panel figure's canvas and mark sizes. It keeps V3's
labels, title, colors, shapes, solid line types, x positions/offsets, childhood
shading, zero reference, typography, y range and exact reveal sequence. V3 and
all its builds remain unchanged. No values, intervals or analysis are computed
again for V4; the same plot function and data supply every mark.

The compact canvas is **14 × 9.5 inches** (previously 22 × 8.5). All four lines
increase from 2.1 to **3.3 mm**, point size from 6.2 to **10 mm**, and the black
outline stroke from 1.15 to **2.2 mm**. Main and build plots remain free of CIs;
the separate CI backup has the same compact geometry and unchanged intervals.

```{r single-sensitivity-onepanel-v4, fig.width=14, fig.height=9.5}
single_onepanel_v4 = list(width = 14, height = 9.5,
                         line_width = 3.3, point_size = 10, point_stroke = 2.2)
plot_single_sensitivity_onepanel_v4 = function(step = 5L, with_ci = FALSE) {

}
p.single.onepanel.v4 = save_presentation_v2_family(

    "build03_add_fault_childhood", "build04_add_punish_childhood", "build05_add_adults_full"),
  width = single_onepanel_v4$width, height = single_onepanel_v4$height)
p.single.onepanel.v4$main
p.single.onepanel.v4$backup
p.single.onepanel.v4$builds[[1]]

# Only linewidth, size and stroke may differ from the corresponding V3 layers.
# This also checks unchanged colors, shapes, values and alpha/reveal sequences.
for (step in 0:5) {
  for (with_ci in c(FALSE, TRUE)) {
    old = ggplot_build(plot_single_sensitivity_onepanel(step, with_ci))
    new = ggplot_build(plot_single_sensitivity_onepanel_v4(step, with_ci))
    stopifnot(identical(old$layout$layout, new$layout$layout),
              identical(old$layout$panel_params[[1]]$x.range, new$layout$panel_params[[1]]$x.range),
              identical(old$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y.range, new$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y.range),
              identical(old$layout$panel_params[[1]]$x$get_breaks(), new$layout$panel_params[[1]]$x$get_breaks()),
              identical(old$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y$get_breaks(), new$layout$panel_params[[1]]$y$get_breaks()))
    for (layer in seq_along(old$data)) {
      retained_columns = setdiff(names(old$data[[layer]]), c("linewidth", "size", "stroke"))
      stopifnot(identical(old$data[[layer]][retained_columns], new$data[[layer]][retained_columns]))
    }
  }
}
stopifnot(check_presentation_builds(p.single.onepanel.v4, c(0L, 2L, 4L, 6L, 8L, 12L)))
```

# Intention sensitivity across causal contexts

This additional companion to the all-measure role-preference figure uses
**100 × (Intentional mean Yes − Accidental mean Yes)**. The four panels are
Caused, Lexical, Fault and Punish; the three trajectories are Single Cause,
Chain: Distal and Chain: Proximal. Study 1 is absent because it does not
manipulate intention. A negative value means more Yes in Accidental.

Reuse the existing scenario-averaged participant means and stage groups.
Conditions contain different people, so subtract group means rather than
inventing within-participant intention contrasts. All 12 Single Cause effects
and intervals are reused exactly. The 24 chain intervals apply the same
5,000-replicate procedure within stage: independently resample Intentional and
Accidental participants, keeping both roles and all four measures together on
each sampled row. A separate fixed seed leaves every earlier interval intact.

Chain: Proximal describes judgments of the proximal agent **when the distal
agent's intention changes**, not a manipulation of the proximal agent's own
intention. The source-study cohorts remain different; these are descriptive,
cross-sectional comparisons rather than a test isolating causal context.

```{r context-sensitivity-summary}
df.chain.sensitivity.means = df.stage.means %>% filter(study == "Study 2")
chain_score_order = expand_grid(role = role_order, measure = measure_order) %>%
  transmute(score = paste(role, measure, sep = "__")) %>% pull(score)
df.chain.sensitivity.wide = df.chain.sensitivity.means %>%
  mutate(score = paste(role, measure, sep = "__")) %>%
  select(stage, condition, participant, score, yes_mean) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = score, values_from = yes_mean) %>% arrange(stage, condition, participant)
check_labels(df.chain.sensitivity.means$condition, condition_order, "chain sensitivity condition")
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(df.chain.sensitivity.wide[c("stage", "condition", "participant")]))
RNGkind("Mersenne-Twister", "Inversion", "Rejection")
set.seed(bootstrap_seed + 12L)
chain_sensitivity_intervals = list()
for (stage_name in stage_order) {
  rows = filter(df.chain.sensitivity.wide, stage == stage_name)
  intentional = rows %>% filter(condition == "Intentional") %>% select(all_of(chain_score_order)) %>% as.matrix()
  accidental = rows %>% filter(condition == "Accidental") %>% select(all_of(chain_score_order)) %>% as.matrix()
  stopifnot(nrow(intentional) > 0L, nrow(accidental) > 0L)
  draws = replicate(bootstrap_replicates, {
    i = sample.int(nrow(intentional), replace = TRUE)
    a = sample.int(nrow(accidental), replace = TRUE)
    100 * (apply(intentional[i, , drop = FALSE], 2, mean_available) -
             apply(accidental[a, , drop = FALSE], 2, mean_available))
  })
  chain_sensitivity_intervals[[stage_name]] = tibble(stage = stage_name, score = chain_score_order,
    lower_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .025, na.rm = TRUE),
    upper_pp = apply(draws, 1, quantile, probs = .975, na.rm = TRUE))
}
df.chain.sensitivity.intervals = bind_rows(chain_sensitivity_intervals) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(score, delim = "__", names = c("role", "measure"))
df.chain.sensitivity.summary = df.chain.sensitivity.means %>%
  group_by(stage, condition, measure, role) %>%
  summarise(eligible_n = n(), n = sum(!is.na(yes_mean)), yes_mean = mean_available(yes_mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(eligible_n, n, yes_mean)) %>%
  mutate(mean_pp = 100 * (yes_mean_Intentional - yes_mean_Accidental)) %>%
  left_join(df.chain.sensitivity.intervals, by = c("stage", "measure", "role"), relationship = "one-to-one") %>%
  mutate(study = "Study 2", context = paste0("Chain: ", role), contrast = "Intentional minus Accidental") %>%
  select(-role)
df.context.sensitivity.summary = bind_rows(
  df.single.sensitivity.summary %>% mutate(context = "Single Cause"), df.chain.sensitivity.summary) %>%
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = stage_order), measure = factor(measure, levels = measure_order),
         context = factor(context, levels = stage_target_order)) %>%
  select(study, stage, context, contrast, measure, eligible_n_Intentional, eligible_n_Accidental,
         n_Intentional, n_Accidental, yes_mean_Intentional, yes_mean_Accidental, mean_pp, lower_pp, upper_pp) %>%
  arrange(stage, measure, context)
stopifnot(nrow(df.context.sensitivity.summary) == 36L,
          !anyNA(df.context.sensitivity.summary),
          !anyDuplicated(df.context.sensitivity.summary[c("stage", "measure", "context")]),
          all(dplyr::between(df.context.sensitivity.summary$mean_pp, -100, 100)),
          all(df.context.sensitivity.summary$lower_pp <= df.context.sensitivity.summary$upper_pp))
# Reused Single Cause values and intervals must remain exactly identical.
single_context_check = df.context.sensitivity.summary %>% filter(context == "Single Cause")
for (column in names(df.single.sensitivity.summary)) {
  old = df.single.sensitivity.summary[[column]]
  new = single_context_check[[column]]
  if (is.factor(old)) old = as.character(old)
  if (is.factor(new)) new = as.character(new)
  stopifnot(identical(unname(old), unname(new)))
}
# Independently link each contrast to the already validated role/context means.
df.context.sensitivity.expected = df.stage.summary %>%
  filter(study %in% c("Single Cause", "Study 2")) %>%
  mutate(context = if_else(study == "Single Cause", "Single Cause", paste0("Chain: ", role))) %>%
  select(study, stage, measure, context, condition, checked_mean = mean, checked_n = n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = c(checked_mean, checked_n))
df.context.sensitivity.checked = df.context.sensitivity.summary %>%
  left_join(df.context.sensitivity.expected, by = c("study", "stage", "measure", "context"),
            relationship = "one-to-one")
stopifnot(all(abs(df.context.sensitivity.checked$yes_mean_Intentional -
                   df.context.sensitivity.checked$checked_mean_Intentional) < 1e-12),
          all(abs(df.context.sensitivity.checked$yes_mean_Accidental -
                    df.context.sensitivity.checked$checked_mean_Accidental) < 1e-12),
          all(df.context.sensitivity.checked$n_Intentional == df.context.sensitivity.checked$checked_n_Intentional),
          all(df.context.sensitivity.checked$n_Accidental == df.context.sensitivity.checked$checked_n_Accidental),
          all(abs(df.context.sensitivity.checked$mean_pp - 100 *
                    (df.context.sensitivity.checked$checked_mean_Intentional -
                       df.context.sensitivity.checked$checked_mean_Accidental)) < 1e-10))
```

## Four-panel presentation figure and cumulative builds

The companion reuses the all-measure figure's 22 × 8.5-inch presentation
canvas, large text, outlined marks, childhood shading and strong dashed zero
reference. Gray squares, red circles and blue triangles retain the existing
causal-context palette. A single legend names the contexts explicitly; color
encodes context rather than intention condition or judgment.

Main, CI backup and every build share one y scale derived from all means and
intervals. Main/build versions omit CIs. Build 00 is the full blank scaffold;
01 adds Single Cause childhood, 02 adds Chain: Proximal childhood, 03 adds
Chain: Distal childhood, and 04 adds all Adults. Earlier marks never move.

```{r context-sensitivity-plot, fig.width=22, fig.height=8.5}
# This family uses the same order for its legend and childhood reveals.
# Named color/shape/line mappings stay attached to their original contexts.
context_sensitivity_order = c("Single Cause", "Chain: Proximal", "Chain: Distal")
context_sensitivity_colors = setNames(unname(synthesis_colors), stage_target_order)
context_sensitivity_style = list(
  order = context_sensitivity_order, colors = context_sensitivity_colors, fills = context_sensitivity_colors,
  shapes = setNames(c(22, 21, 24), stage_target_order),
  lines = setNames(c("dotted", "solid", "dashed"), stage_target_order))
context_sensitivity_limits = c(
  floor(min(0, df.context.sensitivity.summary$mean_pp - 5,
            df.context.sensitivity.summary$lower_pp) / 10) * 10,
  ceiling(max(0, df.context.sensitivity.summary$mean_pp + 5,
              df.context.sensitivity.summary$upper_pp) / 10) * 10)
context_sensitivity_breaks = seq(ceiling(context_sensitivity_limits[1] / 25) * 25,
                                 floor(context_sensitivity_limits[2] / 25) * 25, 25)
df.context.sensitivity.plot = df.context.sensitivity.summary %>%
  transmute(panel = as.character(measure), series = as.character(context), stage,
            mean = mean_pp, lower = lower_pp, upper = upper_pp,
            reveal_step = if_else(stage == "Adults", 4L, match(context, context_sensitivity_order)))
plot_context_sensitivity = function(step = 4L, with_ci = FALSE) {
  plot_causal_verbs_talk(df.context.sensitivity.plot, measure_order, context_sensitivity_style,
                         context_sensitivity_limits, context_sensitivity_breaks,
                         "Intentional −
Accidental (%)", 0, step, with_ci)
}
p.context.sensitivity = save_presentation_v2_family(
  plot_context_sensitivity, "intention_sensitivity_across_contexts_talk_v1", "intention_sensitivity_across_contexts",
  c("build00_blank", "build01_single_cause_childhood", "build02_add_chain_proximal_childhood",
    "build03_add_chain_distal_childhood", "build04_add_adults_full"))
```
